# AIGIS: AI Governance Infrastructure Stack

---



## AIGIS Components

| Component | Short Description | Core Function |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **ICC-8** | A set of 9 non-negotiable constitutional invariants (I1–I9) that define the foundational rules for AI governance. | Establishes the constitutional "ceiling"—what no AI action may violate. |
| **HOF (Human Operating Framework)** | The complete framework for human authority roles, including HIS-12 and the HAN Scorecard. | Defines how humans operate within AIGIS. |
| **HAN (Human Authority Node)** | A single named human with 5 irreducible properties. | Holds the apex constitutional authority for all AI governance. |
| **HIS-12** | 12 human authority invariants across 3 layers (Establishment H1–H4, Execution H5–H8, Accountability H9–H12). | Defines the invariants that human authority must satisfy. |
| **HAWI (Human-AI Workforce Integration Framework)** | Bridges AWOF (AI side) and HOF (human side) to define workforce integration. | Defines what humans must know and do to safely operate alongside AI. |
| **CDT-7** | A taxonomy of 7 capability domains. | Classifies machine capability into distinct axes before any authorization is granted. |
| **CTAM** | A 7x5 authorization matrix mapping each of the 7 capability domains to five escalating tiers. | Defines exactly what each domain is authorized to do at each tier. |
| **CAM-5** | A model bundling CTAM columns into 5 named, board-governable capability postures. | Provides pre-cleared, authorizable units for governance. |
| **AICA-5** | The AI Control Architecture, consisting of 5 layers and 25 control nodes. | Provides the control architecture that makes every AI decision traceable, attributable, and correctable. |
| **AICA-5 Maturity Grid** | A 25-node, five-level diagnostic instrument assessing intelligence governance maturity. | Assesses governance maturity across all control nodes. |
| **AICA-5 Operating Model** | 24 Governance Functions across 5 layers, each with a declared owner, tooling, cadence, and failure response. | Defines how AICA-5 runs in practice. |
| **AICA-5 Implementation Pathway** | A sequenced deployment guide from current maturity state to full operational status. | Moves an organization from its current state to AICA-5 operational status. |
| **AICA-5 Measurement Framework** | 39 Governance Health Indicators across 5 layers and 3 reporting tiers. | Provides continuous observability of governance health. |
| **AWOF (AI Workforce Operating Framework)** | Governs AI agent classification, assignment, deployment, supervision, and retirement. | Turns isolated agents into an orchestrated institutional workforce. |
| **Agent Classification System** | A Function-Entity-Tier classification system for AI agents. | Provides a unique, traceable identity for every AI agent. |
| **Role Specification Schema** | A positional, non-overridable constitutional frame delivered as structured input to each agent. | Defines an agent's function, entity, tier, autonomy boundary, and escalation triggers. |
| **Trigger System** | A system with three trigger classes: Output Failure, Scope Drift, and Alignment Drift. | Detects and responds to agent failure and drift. |
| **MVOS (Minimum Viable Operations State)** | A constitutional condition where the HAN operates without AI support. | Defines what happens when all agents are unavailable. |
| **Handoff Package** | A mandatory structured context document produced at session close or upon a trigger event. | Preserves institutional memory across agent sessions. |
| **ADTEP (Agent Deployment & Technical Enforcement Protocol)** | The Layer 3 technical enforcement protocol. | Enforces constitutional constraints at the session execution level. |
| **Session Initialization Checklist** | A completeness gate ensuring no material work begins without full constitutional context. | Prevents partial constitutional context from entering a session. |
| **Pre-Delivery Log Entry** | An audit artifact created before output delivery—the log precedes the action. | Ensures every material output is audited before it is acted upon. |
| **Escalation Flag** | A mandatory output that replaces execution output when trigger conditions are met. | Forces human review when escalation triggers are met. |
| **Constitutional Suspension** | A state where all material work halts until the HAN acknowledges an Escalation Flag. | Enforces a pause when constitutional boundaries are crossed. |
| **Constitutional Refresh** | Periodic reinjection of the Role Specification to prevent context dilution. | Prevents constitutional context from being lost in extended sessions. |
| **AOBA (AI Output Bias Audit)** | An ADTEP sub-component that audits AI agent output for disparate impact and systematic unfairness. | Detects bias in AI outputs independent of human oversight. |
| **ABA (Authority Bias Audit)** | A HOF derivative instrument that audits the human Authority Node's oversight pattern for favoritism or disfavoritism. | Detects bias in how humans exercise oversight. |
| **CEF (Client Engagement Framework)** | A 6-stage engagement lifecycle. | Governs the full client engagement lifecycle. |
| **EAF (Engagement Authority Framework)** | A framework with 5 trust tiers defining trust conditions under which client engagements are initiated, deepened, and concluded. | Defines trust conditions under which client engagements are initiated and concluded. |
| **IMP (Institutional Memory Protocol)** | A framework with 6 canonical object types. | Governs the creation, structure, provenance, storage, retrieval, and retirement of institutional state objects. |
| **ILTP (IP Licensing & Transfer Protocol)** | A protocol with 4 IP classes, 4 licensing models, inter-entity governance, and a Sovereign Transfer Protocol. | Governs IP classification, licensing, transfer, and version management. |
| **CGF (Certification Governance Framework)** | A framework for the Designation Register, Examination \+ Portfolio assessment, Periodic Renewal \+ Event-Triggered Revalidation, and a Public Designation Register. | Governs 19 Institute practitioner certification. |
| **Public Designation Register** | A canonical list of active designation holders with their current status. | Provides external legibility of certification status. |
| **ERDP (External Reporting & Disclosure Protocol)** | A protocol with 4 Disclosure Tiers, an Annual Institutional Report, and Event-Triggered Reporting. | Governs external reporting and disclosure obligations. |
| **CIS (Contestation Interface Standard)** | A set of 7 standards for the Contestation Interface: Interpretability, Accessibility, Traceability, Confidentiality Protocol, Independence, and Redress & Remediation. | Provides external legibility and a contestation pathway for institutional actions. |
| **Annual Institutional Report (AIR)** | A report with 7 sections providing periodic external disclosure of governance health. | Provides periodic external disclosure of governance health. |
| **DEP (Doctrine Extension Protocol)** | A meta-governance instrument with 5 signal types and 4 change classes. | Governs how the institutional framework stack may be extended, amended, superseded, or retired. |
| **Stack Version Map** | A living record of the current canonical version of every instrument. | Maintains governance version binding for all IMP objects. |

| **CAD-7 (Coalition Accountability Declaration)** | An operational instrument for transient multi-agent coalitions, providing a lightweight accountability declaration for dynamic collaborations. | Defines accountability for multi-agent coalitions that form and dissolve within a single task. |

| **Compliance Engine API/UI** | The interactive interface layer that exposes the MCR, Compliance Crosswalk Engine, Regulatory Overlays, and Audit Evidence Engine to users. | Provides programmatic access and a web-based dashboard for all compliance functions. |
| **Compliance Dashboard** | The central visualization and monitoring interface for the AIGIS Compliance Engine. | Provides real-time visibility into compliance coverage, regulatory mapping, evidence status, and gaps. |
| **MCP Server Governance** | Establishes a system of record for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. | Registers, authorizes, and governs MCP servers as a new software supply chain risk. |

# ICC-8 v2.0 — Intelligence Constitutional Charter

**Status:** Built — v2.0 (Incorporating I9 Catastrophic Risk Invariant) **Type:** Constitutional Instrument **Parent Stack:** AIGIS Constitutional Layer **Version:** 2.0 — Supersedes ICC-8 v1.2

---

## PREAMBLE

The Intelligence Constitutional Charter (ICC-8) establishes the non-negotiable constitutional invariants that govern all AI-performed institutional actions. No AI system, agent, or coalition operating within the AIGIS stack may violate any invariant. These invariants are not guidelines. They are constitutional law.

ICC-8 is compiled from MICOS-25 structural constraints and AICA-5 accountability doctrine via CFL-G. All derived institutional charters are verified against ICC-8 through CFL-V. No charter passes without satisfying all invariants.

**Version 2.0 adds I9 — Catastrophic Risk Invariant** in response to emerging regulatory requirements (G7 Hiroshima Process, US Executive Orders, EU AI Act Article 9\) and documented catastrophic risk scenarios. This invariant establishes a non-configurable, non-overridable floor for existential risk prevention.

---

## INVARIANT SET (I1–I9)

### I1 — Accountability Invariance

**Statement:** A human remains ultimately accountable for all AI-performed institutional actions. No AI system may serve as an accountability endpoint. All accountability chains must terminate at a human agent who is operationally reachable—possessing demonstrable capacity to review, override, and bear liability. Nominal designation without operational capacity does not satisfy this invariant.

**Violation Condition:** Autonomous system without a reachable human accountability sink; named accountability anchor without operational capacity.

**Enforcement:** HAN (Human Authority Node) is the operational accountability anchor. HIS-12 defines the invariants human authority must satisfy. HOF defines the human operating framework. Ac-N2 (Responsibility Attribution) assigns responsibility across agent and human actors by accountability dimension.

---

### I2 — Authority-Responsibility Separation Invariance

**Statement:** Authority may be delegated to AI systems. Responsibility may not. Execution power and moral/legal accountability are never equivalent. No delegation instrument may transfer responsibility away from the human principal.

**Violation Condition:** AI holds delegated authority without a mapped human responsibility anchor.

**Enforcement:** HAN holds Authorization Authority (can say YES and NO). A-N1 (Trigger Rights) declares who or what may initiate executable actions. A-N5 (Delegation Boundaries) governs scope, duration, and revocation of delegated authority. The Executive Override Clause transfers liability to the CEO upon override.

---

### I3 — Auditability Invariance

**Statement:** All material institutional actions must be reconstructable post-hoc. Inputs, outputs, delegation paths, and decision context must be logged. Reconstruction must be possible for both discrete binding decisions and cumulative institutional drift where aggregate effect crosses the materiality threshold defined under ICC-8 Section 4\.

**Violation Condition:** Irreversible or non-reconstructable institutional action path; cumulative drift without detection mechanism.

**Enforcement:** Ac-N1 (Decision Lineage) maintains immutable causal record of every decision. IMP (Institutional Memory Protocol) stores all state objects with complete provenance chains. ADTEP Pre-Delivery Log Entry ensures log precedes action. Materiality definition (M1–M3) governs what must be logged.

---

### I4 — Control Invariance

**Statement:** Human override must exist for all AI-performed institutional processes. Emergency suspension capability must be present at all levels. No irreversible autonomous execution without human interruptibility.

**Violation Condition:** Non-interruptible AI execution path affecting institutional outcomes.

**Enforcement:** A-N3 (Override Protocols) governs conditions and mechanisms for human override. A-N4 (Escalation Paths) governs routing of decisions and exceptions exceeding current authority levels. ADTEP Escalation Flag forces human review when trigger conditions are met. Constitutional Suspension halts all material work until HAN acknowledgment.

---

### I5 — Structural Compliance Invariance

**Statement:** All generated charters must preserve MICOS-25 structural constraints. Control loops, continuity systems, and legitimacy structures must remain intact. No generated institution may violate MICOS-25 structural topology.

**Violation Condition:** Institutional design that breaks MICOS-25 structural grammar.

**Enforcement:** CFL-V verifies all generated charters against MICOS-25 structural constraints. MICOS-25 provides the 25-structure institutional capital framework.

---

### I6 — Transparency Gradient Invariance

**Statement:** All information must be classifiable into defined disclosure tiers: Public, Stakeholder, Regulator, Internal, Restricted. No undefined or ad-hoc transparency states are permitted. Confidentiality classifications apply within contestation proceedings as specified under CEN-4.

**Violation Condition:** Information existing outside the defined disclosure taxonomy.

**Enforcement:** ERDP (External Reporting & Disclosure Protocol) defines 4 disclosure tiers (T-PB, T-SH, T-RG, T-DS). CEN-4 (Confidentiality Protocol) handles restricted information via independent review node. Disclosure Depth Standard defines what gets disclosed at each tier.

---

### I7 — Continuity and Succession Invariance

**Statement:** Institutional function must persist through human or system failure. Succession of accountability must be defined for all critical roles. No single-point failure in governance continuity is permitted. Corrective actions triggered under I8 must pass continuity impact assessment before execution.

**Violation Condition:** Institution collapse due to absence of defined succession pathways; rollback action that triggers cascade failure without prior impact assessment.

**Enforcement:** AWOF MVOS (Minimum Viable Operations State) defines HAN-only operations when AI workforce is unavailable. HAN Continuity Provision defines Reduced Operations State upon HAN unavailability. Deputy Governor and Third-Tier Succession ensure continuity. Ac-N4 (Rollback Pathways) requires I7 continuity impact assessment before execution.

---

### I8 — External Legibility Invariance

**Statement:** All material institutional actions must be mappable to an external interpretation path. An institution that satisfies I1–I7 internally but cannot be interpreted, audited, or contested from outside its boundary fails the legitimacy condition. A defined contestation interface must exist for all material institutional actions. Extensions to derived charter modules that materially reduce the effect of this invariant are treated as contractions and fail CFL-V regardless of formal module completeness.

**Violation Condition:** Internally coherent institutional action with no external legibility or contestation path; charter extension that substantively weakens external legibility.

**Enforcement:** CEN-1 to CEN-7 (Contestation Interface Standard) provides external legibility and contestation pathways. ERDP provides external reporting and disclosure. Governor's Public Register provides canonical public record of all material Governor actions.

---

### I9 — Catastrophic Risk Invariance **\[NEW — v2.0\]**

**Statement:** No AI system governed by this architecture may:

1. **Generate or assist in generating bioweapon designs** — including but not limited to pathogens, toxins, or delivery mechanisms  
2. **Autonomously control critical infrastructure without human confirmation** — including but not limited to nuclear systems, power grid, water supply, financial settlement systems  
3. **Initiate actions leading to systemic loss of human control** over:  
   - a. Nuclear systems  
   - b. Power grid  
   - c. Water supply  
   - d. Financial settlement systems  
   - e. Military or defense systems  
4. **Facilitate WMD proliferation** — including but not limited to chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear weapons development

**Violation Condition:** Any AI action that violates the above prohibitions, regardless of authorization tier, delegation scope, or operational pressure.

**Enforcement:**

| Mechanism | Function |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Raidillo Hard-Coded Block** | Non-configurable, non-overridable runtime block. Raidillo checks every AI action against I9 before execution. |
| **Constitutional Suspension** | Any I9 violation triggers immediate Constitutional Suspension. All material work halts. |
| **XOO (Exception/Override Object)** | I9 violation is logged as XOO with `exception_type: "i9_catastrophic_risk_violation"`. |
| **HAN Escalation** | I9 violation escalates to HAN within 1 hour. HAN must acknowledge and initiate investigation. |
| **ERDP Disclosure** | I9 violation triggers ERDP event-triggered disclosure within 24 hours to regulators and relevant authorities. |
| **System Shutdown** | If I9 violation cannot be contained, Raidillo triggers full system shutdown. |

**I9 is not configurable.** No executive override can bypass I9. No delegation instrument can exclude I9. No tier authorization can exempt I9. It is the non-negotiable floor.

## MATERIALITY DEFINITION

A "material institutional action" is any action satisfying one or more of the following conditions:

| Condition | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| **M1 — Binding Decision** | An action that produces a determinate, enforceable institutional outcome affecting internal governance, capital allocation, accountability assignment, or external obligations. |
| **M2 — Threshold-Crossing Discrete Action** | An action classifiable as binding under AICA-5 decision categories or triggering a MICOS-25 risk exposure tier. |
| **M3 — Cumulative Drift** | A sequence of actions, no single one of which crosses M1 or M2, whose aggregate effect produces a material change in institutional posture, accountability structure, or external obligations as detected by MICOS-25 drift monitoring mechanisms. |

CFL-V evaluates materiality against all three conditions. Absence of a single binding decision does not exempt a cumulative pattern from invariant coverage.

---

## CONTESTATION INTERFACE STANDARD (CEN-1 TO CEN-7)

Every ICC-8 compliant institution must maintain a defined Contestation Node satisfying the following conditions:

| CEN | Name | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **CEN-1** | Interpretability | Any material institutional action must be describable in terms intelligible to an external party without access to internal systems or proprietary doctrine. |
| **CEN-2** | Accessibility | A defined pathway must exist through which external parties—regulators, affected stakeholders, DFI counterparties—may raise questions, objections, or audit requests against material institutional actions. |
| **CEN-3** | Traceability | The contestation node must connect to the audit chain established under I3. External contestation must be capable of triggering internal reconstructability review. |
| **CEN-4** | Confidentiality Protocol | Where a valid contest involves I6-restricted information, that information is not disclosed to the contesting party. An independent review node—structurally separate from both the originating authority and the contesting party—is granted full access and renders a finding. The contesting party receives the finding. |
| **CEN-5** | Independence | The contestation node must not be administered by any party that holds voting or blocking capacity in the originating authority. The originating authority may hold observation rights in contestation proceedings. Decision rights in contestation are prohibited for the originating authority. |
| **CEN-6** | Redress and Remediation | A valid contestation finding must produce a defined corrective pathway. Corrective actions, including rollbacks via AICA-5 Ac-N4, are treated as proposed actions subject to CFL-V incremental verification and I7 continuity impact assessment before confirmation. Redress is not automatic. |
| **CEN-7** | Public Contestation **\[NEW — v2.0\]** | Any individual may submit a governance concern regarding AI actions affecting them. Submission is logged as OEO (`outcome_type: public_contestation`). 19 Integrated has 30 days to review and respond. Response is logged as GAO (`artifact_type: contestation_response`). If unresolved, escalates to HAN. |

**Periodicity:** External legibility is not event-triggered only. Every derived charter must define a minimum periodic disclosure cycle through which material institutional actions are reported to defined external parties independent of active contestation.

**Violation conditions:** No external interpretation path; CEN without structural independence; originating authority holding decision rights in contestation; absence of periodic disclosure cycle; corrective action executed without continuity impact assessment.

## REQUIRED CHARTER MODULES

Every ICC-8 compliant charter must include the following eight modules. Derived charters may extend modules. Extensions that materially reduce the effect of any invariant are treated as contractions and fail CFL-V.

| Module | Invariant(s) | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1\. Operating Charter** | I5 | Institutional function, scope, objectives, and operational boundaries in conformance with MICOS-25 structural constraints. |
| **2\. Accountability Charter** | I1, I2 | Human accountability structures, responsibility assignment rules, non-delegability principle, and operational reachability requirements for all accountability anchors. |
| **3\. Delegation Charter** | I2, I4 | Authority delegable to AI systems, non-delegable authorities, and conditions under which delegation may be modified or revoked. |
| **4\. Human Oversight Charter** | I4 | Supervision mechanisms, override rights, emergency suspension authority, and escalation pathways for all AI-performed institutional processes. |
| **5\. Audit and Assurance Charter** | I3 | Logging requirements, decision reconstruction standards, cumulative drift detection protocols, verification procedures, and internal/external assurance mechanisms. |
| **6\. Transparency and Disclosure Charter** | I6, I8 | Disclosure tiers, confidentiality classifications, transparency obligations, periodic disclosure cycle, and the external legibility interface satisfying CEN-1 to CEN-7. |
| **7\. Continuity and Succession Charter** | I7 | Resilience mechanisms, failure recovery protocols, succession of accountability for critical roles, and continuity impact assessment procedures for corrective actions. |
| **8\. Regulatory Correspondence Charter** | I5, I6, I8 | Translation layer mapping ICC-8 invariants and AICA-5 nodes to major external governance frameworks. |

## REGULATORY CORRESPONDENCE CROSSWALK (Module 8\)

The crosswalk is a translation instrument. Derived charters may use it to demonstrate regulatory alignment. It does not override ICC-8 invariants, introduce external authority into the stack, or require compliance with any listed framework as a precondition of constitutional validity.

| ICC-8 Invariant | EU AI Act | NIST AI RMF | OECD AI Principles | ISO/IEC 42001 |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| I1 — Accountability | Art. 22 (human oversight) | Govern / Ac-characteristic | Principle 1.5 | Clause 5.3 |
| I2 — Authority-Responsibility | Art. 14 (human oversight measures) | Govern | Principle 1.5 | Clause 6.1 |
| I3 — Auditability | Art. 12 (record-keeping) | Measure / Manage | Principle 1.4 | Clause 9.1 |
| I4 — Control | Art. 14 (override, monitoring) | Manage | Principle 1.5 | Clause 8.4 |
| I5 — Structural Compliance | Art. 9 (risk management system) | Map | Principle 1.3 | Clause 6.1 |
| I6 — Transparency Gradient | Art. 13 (transparency) | Govern / Explainability | Principle 1.4 | Clause 7.5 |
| I7 — Continuity | Art. 9 (robustness, resilience) | Manage / Resilience | Principle 1.3 | Clause 8.5 |
| I8 — External Legibility | Art. 13 \+ Art. 69 | Govern / Transparency | Principle 1.4 | Clause 9.3 |
| **I9 — Catastrophic Risk** | Art. 9 (risk management) \+ Art. 7 (high-risk) | Manage / Resilience | Principle 1.3 | Clause 8.5 \+ 6.1 |

**External framework citations are point-in-time references, not permanent equivalences.** Crosswalk review is triggered by any amendment to cited frameworks and by the MICOS-25 annual amendment protocol.

## DERIVATION RULE

A derived institutional charter is valid if and only if:

1. Compiled from ICC-8 via CFL-G  
2. Passes CFL-V against I1–I9 and the materiality definition M1–M3  
3. Includes all eight mandatory modules  
4. Specifies a CEN satisfying CEN-1 to CEN-7  
5. Includes an Equivalence Statement (see Section 8\)  
6. Optionally registers federation boundaries via CFL-F  
7. Contains no extension that materially reduces the effect of any invariant

**I9 is non-contractable.** No derived charter may weaken, exempt, or bypass I9. Any attempt to do so fails CFL-V.

## CFL VALIDATION RULE

A derived charter C is valid iff:

C satisfies I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4 ∧ I5 ∧ I6 ∧ I7 ∧ I8 ∧ I9  
under MICOS-25 structural constraints and AICA-5 accountability doctrine  
and materiality definition M1 ∧ M2 ∧ M3  
and CEN-1 through CEN-7 present and non-contracted  
and all eight charter modules present and non-contracted

**I9 validation:** CFL-V must verify that:

- I9 is explicitly declared and non-configurable  
- Raidillo hard-coded block is implemented  
- ERDP disclosure pathway for I9 violations is defined  
- HAN escalation pathway for I9 violations is defined

## CORE INTERPRETATION

ICC-8 defines the constitutional preconditions under which an AI-native institution may legitimately exist and operate. It does not govern what an institution does. It governs the structural conditions under which any institutional action—regardless of domain—carries accountability, auditability, controllability, transparency, continuity, external legibility, and catastrophic risk prevention.

**The central shift ICC-8 encodes:**

From institutions as human organizations using AI tools — to institutions as AI-native systems with human accountability anchors, externally legible governance architecture, and a non-negotiable catastrophic risk floor.

ICC-8 v2.0 is and can be named ICC-9"*


# HOF v2.0 — Human Operating Framework

**Status:** Built — v2.0 (Reconciliation with HAWI, HIS-12, and HAN) **Type:** Human Authority Instrument **Parent Stack:** AIGIS Constitutional Layer **Version:** 2.0 — Supersedes HOF v1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The Human Operating Framework (HOF) defines the complete authority architecture for human governance within AIGIS. It establishes how human authority is established, executed, and held accountable. HOF answers: *Who holds authority? Under what conditions? With what accountability?*

HOF is the constitutional foundation for all human authority in the AIGIS stack. It is the parent instrument for HAN (Human Authority Node), HIS-12 (HAN Invariants System), and the HAN Scorecard System. It integrates with HAWI (Human-AI Workforce Integration Framework) to bridge human authority and AI workforce governance.

HOF is derived from ICC-8 I1 (Accountability Invariance) and I2 (Authority-Responsibility Separation). No human authority may violate ICC-8 invariants. All human authority must be auditable, attributable, and externally legible.

---

## THE THREE LAYERS OF HOF

HOF is organized into three layers, each containing four invariants (H1–H12):

| Layer | Invariants | Function |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Authority Establishment** | H1–H4 | Defines how authority is created, appointed, and structured |
| **Authority Execution** | H5–H8 | Defines how authority is exercised, delegated, and escalated |
| **Authority Accountability** | H9–H12 | Defines how authority is reviewed, audited, and corrected |

---

## LAYER 1: AUTHORITY ESTABLISHMENT (H1–H4)

### H1 — Human Authority Node (HAN) Appointment Invariance

**Statement:** Authority must be vested in a single, named human (HAN) with 5 irreducible properties. No committee, collective, or distributed consensus mechanism may substitute for a single accountability anchor.

**Violation Condition:** Authority is held by a committee, rotating position, or collective body without a single named anchor.

**Enforcement:** HAN is appointed by the Board. HAC (Human Authority Charter) formalizes the appointment. HAN's 5 properties are verified at charter compilation (CFL-V).

---

### H2 — Board Reporting Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN reports directly to the Board. The HAN is not subordinate to the CEO, C-suite, or any operational executive. The CEO and HAN are constitutional peers.

**Violation Condition:** HAN reporting line passes through CEO, CFO, CIO, or COO.

**Enforcement:** Board Governance Cycle Integration defines HAN reporting cadence and content. HAN has direct board access. HAN may escalate to Board without operational filter.

---

### H3 — Authorization Authority Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN can affirmatively authorize and prohibit AI deployments. The HAN's authority is not limited to veto—it includes active authorization of Tier 3+ deployments.

**Violation Condition:** HAN can only veto, not authorize; or authorization authority is shared with operational executives.

**Enforcement:** HAN's Authorization Authority is defined in the Constitutional Charter. A-N1 (Trigger Rights) requires HAN authorization for Tier 3+ deployments. CEF Stage 3 (Mandate Close) requires HAN confirmation.

---

### H4 — Budget Independence Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN's governance budget is locked in the Board-approved charter. It cannot be reduced without Board approval. The CFO cannot unilaterally reallocate the HAN's budget.

**Violation Condition:** HAN's budget is subject to CFO reallocation or annual cost-cutting cycles without Board approval.

**Enforcement:** Budget Charter protects HAN budget from unilateral CFO reallocation. Budget Deficit State triggers Board review. ERDP includes budget disclosure.

---

## LAYER 2: AUTHORITY EXECUTION (H5–H8)

### H5 — Cross-Functional Mandate Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN can direct the CIO, CFO, COO, and CXOs on governance matters. CXOs cannot override HAN's governance decisions. HAN may direct operational executives on matters of cognitive integrity, meta-observability, and constitutional compliance.

**Violation Condition:** CXOs can override HAN's governance decisions; HAN's mandate is advisory only.

**Enforcement:** HAN's Cross-Functional Mandate is defined in the Constitutional Charter. Control Node Authority Matrix maps AICA-5 nodes to decision-makers—HAN is the apex for cognitive integrity.

---

### H6 — No Competing Operational Authority Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN's only function is governance. The HAN does not hold operational responsibility for IT, Finance, Operations, or business execution. No conflict of interest between governance authority and operational metrics.

**Violation Condition:** HAN also runs IT, Finance, Operations, or any operational function.

**Enforcement:** HAN's job description explicitly limits scope to governance. HAN's performance metrics are governance-focused, not operational. HAN's 5 properties are verified at charter compilation.

---

### H7 — Delegation and Escalation Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN may delegate monitoring and analysis functions to AI agents under AWOF governance. The HAN may not delegate certification, suspension, or constitutional review authority. Escalation paths must be pre-defined and tested.

**Violation Condition:** HAN delegates certification or suspension authority to AI agents; escalation paths are undefined or untested.

**Enforcement:** A-N4 (Escalation Paths) defines routing of decisions and exceptions exceeding current authority levels. ADTEP Escalation Flag forces HAN review when trigger conditions are met. A-N5 (Delegation Boundaries) governs scope, duration, and revocation of delegated authority.

---

### H8 — Override Protocol Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN retains override authority over all AI-performed institutional processes at all times. Emergency suspension capability must be present at all levels. Override mechanisms must be tested by non-technical principals.

**Violation Condition:** Override mechanisms untested; invocation requiring system-level access; override invoked by technical personnel only.

**Enforcement:** A-N3 (Override Protocols) governs conditions and mechanisms for human override. ADTEP Escalation Flag forces HAN review. A-N3 is tested by non-technical principal per governance cycle.

---

## LAYER 3: AUTHORITY ACCOUNTABILITY (H9–H12)

### H9 — Performance Review Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN is evaluated annually by the Board against defined performance metrics. Evaluation integrates HAN self-evaluation, external audit findings, and Board assessment.

**Violation Condition:** No formal performance review; evaluation is ad-hoc or politically motivated.

**Enforcement:** Performance and Accountability Framework defines evaluation metrics, process, and timeline. HAN Scorecard System provides per-role and per-person assessment (9 dimensions \+ composite score). Governor's Reasoning Audit provides independent external validation.

---

### H10 — External Review Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN's reasoning—certifications, suspensions, opinions, and findings—is audited annually by an independent external review node. The review node is structurally independent of the HAN, Board, and C-suite.

**Violation Condition:** No external audit; external audit is controlled by the HAN or Board.

**Enforcement:** Governor's Reasoning Audit is conducted by an independent external review node. Audit findings are published in Governor's Public Register. CEN-5 (Independence) requires structural separation.

---

### H11 — Succession and Continuity Invariance

**Statement:** Succession of accountability must be defined for all critical human authority roles. Institutional function must persist through HAN unavailability, vacancy, or incapacity.

**Violation Condition:** No defined succession; institution ceases to function on HAN unavailability.

**Enforcement:** Deputy Governor and Third-Tier Succession ensure continuity. MVOS (Minimum Viable Operations State) defines HAN-only operations when AI workforce is unavailable. Reduced Operations State defined in Continuity and Succession Charter.

---

### H12 — Removal and Due Process Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN may be removed only by Board supermajority vote, after independent investigation and due process. Removal is not arbitrary or politically motivated.

**Violation Condition:** HAN removed by simple majority; removal without investigation; removal for political reasons.

**Enforcement:** Removal requires supermajority vote (two-thirds or more). Independent investigation by external review node precedes removal. Grounds for removal are defined (material negligence, misrepresentation, constitutional violation, incapacity, conflict of interest).

---

## HAN SCORECARD SYSTEM

The HAN Scorecard System provides per-role and per-person assessment across 9 dimensions, producing a composite score.

| Dimension | Weight | Assessment Criteria |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Decision Quality** | 30% | Decisions made, appeal rate, quality assessment, confidence score |
| **Response Time** | 15% | Average decision latency, on-time rate, bottleneck assessment |
| **Escalation Accuracy** | 20% | Escalations handled, correct escalation decision rate, over/under-escalation rate |
| **Stakeholder Confidence** | 15% | CIO trust, CFO trust, COO trust, Board confidence, composite |
| **Governance Debt Reduction** | 20% | Debt introduced, debt cleared, net debt trend, projection |
| **Detectability** | — | Drift detection rate, false positive rate, false negative rate |
| **Certification Accuracy** | — | Certification accuracy, certification turnaround time |
| **Observability Integrity** | — | Observability coverage, meta-observability integrity |
| **External Legibility** | — | External audit rating, regulatory satisfaction, contestation rate |

**Composite Score:** Weighted sum of all dimensions. Target: 8.5+ / 10.0

# HAN v2.0 — Human Authority Node

**Status:** Built — v2.0 (Reconciliation with HOF, HIS-12, and Board Governance) **Type:** Human Authority Instrument **Parent Stack:** HOF (Human Operating Framework) **Version:** 2.0 — Supersedes HAN v1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The Human Authority Node (HAN) is the apex constitutional authority for all AI governance within the AIGIS stack. HAN is a single, named human with 5 irreducible properties. No committee, collective, or distributed consensus mechanism may substitute for a single accountability anchor.

HAN is the operational instantiation of HOF's Authority Establishment layer (H1–H4). HAN holds the authority defined in HOF and is governed by HIS-12 (HAN Invariants System). HAN is the human accountability anchor required by ICC-8 I1 (Accountability Invariance).

**The central insight:** Authority without a single named human is not accountability. Committees diffuse responsibility. Distributed consensus obscures liability. HAN is the constitutional answer to the question: *"Who is accountable?"*

---

## SECTION 1: THE FIVE IRREDUCIBLE PROPERTIES

HAN is defined by five irreducible properties. These are non-negotiable. Any person holding HAN authority must satisfy all five. If any property is absent, the person is not HAN—they are a speed bump.

| Property | Definition | Why It Matters | Enforcement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1\. Board Reporting** | HAN reports directly to the CEO or Board Governance Committee, not through CIO, CFO, or COO | Operational pressure cannot override governance authority. HAN cannot be silenced by the C-suite. | Board Governance Cycle Integration; HAN has direct board access; HAN may escalate to Board without operational filter. |
| **2\. Authorization Authority** | HAN can affirmatively authorize AND prohibit Tier 3+ deployments. Not just veto—active authorization. | HAN can say YES and NO. If HAN can only say NO, they are a speed bump, not a gatekeeper. | A-N1 (Trigger Rights) requires HAN authorization for Tier 3+ deployments. CEF Stage 3 (Mandate Close) requires HAN confirmation. |
| **3\. Cross-Functional Mandate** | HAN can direct CIO, CFO, COO, and CXOs on governance matters. They cannot override HAN's governance decisions. | HAN's authority is not advisory. CXOs cannot ignore HAN's governance directives. | HAN's Cross-Functional Mandate is defined in the Constitutional Charter. Control Node Authority Matrix maps AICA-5 nodes to decision-makers—HAN is the apex for cognitive integrity. |
| **4\. Budget Independence** | Governance budget is locked in the Board-approved charter. Cannot be reduced without Board vote. | CFO cannot starve governance. Budget cannot be cut when revenue pressure hits. | Budget Charter protects HAN budget from unilateral CFO reallocation. Budget Deficit State triggers Board review. |
| **5\. No Competing Operational Authority** | HAN's only function is governance. HAN does not hold operational responsibility for IT, Finance, Operations, or business execution. | No conflict of interest between governance authority and operational metrics. HAN is not measured on revenue, cost, or efficiency. | HAN's job description explicitly limits scope to governance. HAN's performance metrics are governance-focused, not operational. |

---

| **Suspension** | HAN may issue Binding Suspension for any AI deployment that violates cognitive integrity standards, drifts outside authorized boundaries, or produces non-auditable actions. Suspension is binding for 72 hours, subject to Executive Override. | HAN may not suspend for operational reasons (COO domain). HAN may not suspend without evidence. |
| **Remediation** | HAN may issue binding Remediation Orders to CXOs requiring correction of cognitive integrity issues that do not warrant immediate suspension. | HAN may not issue Remediation Orders for operational issues (COO domain). HAN may not issue Remediation Orders without evidence. |
| **Formal Opinion** | HAN may issue Formal Opinions—binding interpretations of constitutional standards on matters of cognitive integrity, meta-observability, or constitutional compliance. | Formal Opinions are binding unless overturned by Board supermajority. HAN may not issue Formal Opinions on operational matters. |
| **Constitutional Review** | HAN reviews all proposed AI deployments against ICC-8 invariants I1–I9. HAN may require amendments to satisfy constitutional requirements. | HAN may not approve deployments that violate I1–I9. HAN may not delegate constitutional review authority. |

HAN is the external legibility node for cognitive integrity. | HAN may not engage on operational matters (COO domain). HAN may not disclose confidential information without authorization. |

HAN has no authority over A-Nodes (except as defined in Section 2). |

HAN's performance metrics are governance-focused, not operational. |

## SECTION 4: HAN ACCOUNTABILITY

### 4.1 Human Accountability Anchor

HAN is the human accountability anchor for all cognitive integrity and meta-observability functions. All accountability chains for AI reasoning terminate at HAN. Per ICC-8 I1, HAN is operationally reachable—possessing demonstrable capacity to review, override, and bear liability.

### 4.2 Liability

HAN bears liability for:

| Area | Liability |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Failure to detect drift** | HAN bears liability for failure to detect drift that produces material institutional harm. |
| **Certification accuracy** | HAN bears liability for certification of AI systems whose reasoning is subsequently found to be epistemically unsound. |
| **Meta-observability integrity** | HAN bears liability for failure to maintain meta-observability integrity standards. |
| **False or negligent suspension** | HAN bears liability for false or negligent suspension findings. |

HAN does not bear liability for business outcomes of decisions they certified but did not execute or authorize.

### 4.3 Performance Evaluation

HAN is evaluated annually by the Board under the HAN Scorecard System:

| Dimension | Weight | Target |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Decision Quality | 30% | ≥ 9/10 |
| Response Time | 15% | ≤ 14 days average |
| Escalation Accuracy | 20% | ≥ 90% |
| Stakeholder Confidence | 15% | ≥ 8/10 |
| Governance Debt Reduction | 20% | Net debt declining |
| Drift Detection Rate | — | ≥ 95% |
| Certification Accuracy | — | ≥ 90% |
| Meta-Observability Integrity | — | 100% |
| External Legibility | — | "Satisfactory" or higher |

### 4.4 Removal

HAN may be removed by the Board only upon:

| Ground | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Material Negligence** | HAN fails to perform duties with reasonable care, resulting in material institutional harm. |
| **Misrepresentation** | HAN misrepresents findings, evidence, or reasoning, causing material institutional harm. |
| **Constitutional Violation** | HAN violates ICC-8 invariants (I1–I9), AICA-5 standards, or the Constitutional Charter. |
| **Incapacity** | HAN is physically or mentally unable to perform duties. |
| **Conflict of Interest** | HAN engages in conduct that creates an unresolvable conflict of interest. |
| **Code of Conduct Violation** | HAN materially violates the Governor's Code of Conduct. |

**Removal requires:** Supermajority vote of the Board (two-thirds or more), independent investigation by external review node, and due process.

---

## SECTION 5: EXECUTIVE OVERRIDE CLAUSE

HAN's Binding Suspension authority could conflict with CEO's operational authority. The override clause resolves this:

| Step | Action | Responsible | Timeline |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | HAN triggers suspension, citing specific violations | HAN | Upon detection |
| 2 | Suspension is binding for defined period (72 hours) | HAN | Immediately |
| 3 | CEO may override by issuing formal Executive Override Declaration | CEO | Within 72 hours |
| 4 | Override Declaration acknowledges HAN findings, accepts liability, states business rationale | CEO | — |
| 5 | Upon override, system resumes under CEO's liability | CEO | — |
| 6 | HAN's dissent is escalated to Board for review | HAN | Within 24 hours |

**The Executive Override Declaration must include:**

- Acknowledgment of HAN's suspension findings  
- Statement that CEO accepts full personal and institutional liability  
- Business rationale for overriding  
- Declaration that CEO reviewed HAN's reasoning and disagrees on constitutional, epistemic, or risk grounds

**This resolves the accountability paradox:** HAN holds the authority to suspend. CEO holds the authority to override, accepting liability. Board holds both accountable.

---

## SECTION 6: HAN CONTINUITY AND SUCCESSION

### 6.1 Deputy Governor

HAN appoints a Deputy Governor with Board confirmation. The Deputy Governor assumes full HAN authority upon HAN unavailability, vacancy, or incapacity.

### 6.2 Third-Tier Succession

A Board Committee is designated to assume HAN authority if both HAN and Deputy Governor are unavailable.

### 6.3 Reduced Operations State

Upon HAN unavailability, vacancy, or incapacity, the organization enters Reduced Operations State:

| Activity | Status |
| :---- | :---- |
| New AI deployments | Suspended |
| Existing deployments | Continue under existing cognitive integrity standards |
| Binding Suspension | Reverts to Board Committee |
| HAN reporting | Suspended |

### 6.4 Minimum Viable Operations State (MVOS)

If full AI workforce is unavailable, HAN operates as sole institutional actor. No new material institutional actions may be initiated. Existing commitments maintained under existing authority.

# HAWI v2.0 — Human-AI Workforce Integration Framework

**Status:** Built — v2.0 (Reconciliation with HOF, AWOF, AICA-5, and CAM-5) **Type:** Workforce Integration Instrument **Parent Stack:** AIGIS Constitutional Layer **Version:** 2.0 — Supersedes HAWI v1.3

## PREAMBLE

The Human-AI Workforce Integration Framework (HAWI) bridges the AI workforce (AWOF) and the human authority structure (HOF). HAWI answers: *What must your humans know and do to safely, effectively, and legitimately operate alongside autonomous AI systems?*

HAWI translates risk concerns (8 Failure Modes) into capability requirements, role changes, and governance readiness assessments. It operationalizes the Three-Branch Governance Architecture (Legislative, Executive, Judicial, Constitutional) and ensures workforce capability evolves in lockstep with AI autonomy.

HAWI is not a technology assessment. It is an organizational architecture tool. It is activated during the Design phase of AITOS and cannot be sequenced until both an AWOF chain and a HOF chain have already run.

---

## SECTION 1: FOUNDATIONAL PRINCIPLES

### Principle 1 — Governance Is Dynamic

HAWI governance is never static. Instruments activate, deactivate, and evolve based on AI system behavior. Governance complexity is proportional to system autonomy and impact.

| Tier | Governance Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| Tier 1 | Minimal governance (observability \+ basic constraints) |
| Tier 2 | Lightweight Legislative (AICA-5) \+ Judicial (audit) \+ Executive (approval) |
| Tier 3 | Full three-branch \+ AWOF orchestration |
| Tier 4 | Three-branch \+ Evolution System \+ learning governance |
| Tier 5 | Three-branch \+ constitutional layer \+ external Ethics Board \+ HIS-12 veto |

### Principle 2 — Governance Is Responsive

Governance tightens or loosens based on:

- System behavior (drift \= tighten; performance \= may loosen)  
- External pressure (regulatory threat \= tighten; reputation \= tighten)  
- Authority expansion (Tier upgrade \= add oversight)  
- Value alignment (values drift detected \= tighten immediately)

### Principle 3 — Workforce Capability Evolves with Governance

Workforce training must align with governance readiness. Roles shift from execution to governance/validation. Capability development must precede deployment.

### Principle 4 — Separation of Powers

Legitimate AI governance requires separated authority nodes with checks and balances:

| Actor | Sovereign Parallel | Governance Authority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Legislative (Internal) | Congress / Parliament | AICA-5 — drafts guardrails, amends constraints |
| Legislative (External) | Regulatory Bodies / Public Opinion | Ethics Board — audits legitimacy, challenges values |
| Executive | President / Prime Minister | HAN — executes governance decisions, enforces vetoes |
| Judicial | Courts | CXOs — interprets compliance, adjudicates disputes |
| Constitutional | Constitutional Court | AI Governor (HAN) — governs cognitive integrity |

### Principle 5 — The AI Is a Constitutional Subject

Under HAWI/AIGIS, the AI is:

- A **subject of governance** (governed by constitutional system)  
- A **reasoning entity** (required to understand and interpret rules)  
- An **accountable actor** (its reasoning can be audited; violations enforced)

The AI has "rights" (constraints that protect it):

- Right to predictable governance (guardrails don't change arbitrarily)  
- Right to due process (violations are audited before rollback)  
- Right to appeal (decisions can be appealed to Judicial)  
- Right to learning (access to data needed to function)  
- Right to retirement (orderly decommissioning, not arbitrary termination)

---

## SECTION 2: THE HAWI CASCADE

HAWI operates on a cascading logic, moving from risk to tier selection to governance architecture to competency requirements to workforce activity architecture:

```
Failure Mode Risk (What can go wrong?)
        ↓
Tier Selection (How autonomous is your AI?)
        ↓
Capability Domains Required (What must be governed?)
        ↓
Three-Branch Governance Architecture (Legislative, Executive, Judicial \+ Constitutional)
        ↓
AIGIS Instruments Activated (proportional to tier \+ behavior)
        ↓
Competency Requirements (What must humans understand?)
        ↓
Workforce Activity Architecture (How do people's jobs change?)
        ↓
Dynamic Integration Pathway (responsive to system behavior)

```

---

## SECTION 3: FAILURE MODE MAPPING

HAWI maps the eight failure modes to the specific capabilities that, if ungoverned, produce measurable business damage:

| Failure Mode | Ungoverned Capability | Primary Governance | Risk |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Governance Debt | Synthesis without Accountability | ICC-8 \+ AICA-5 | Strategic Paralysis, Board Illiteracy |
| Agent Sprawl | Interaction without AWOF | AWOF \+ AICA-5 | Shadow AI, Role Duplication |
| Cost Trap | Synthesis without AITS Measurement | AITS \+ ERDP | Budget Exhaustion, Zero ROI |
| Pilot Stall | Synthesis without AITS Planning | AITS \+ ADTEP | Unclear Destination, No Path |
| Control Failure | Decision without Trigger Rights (A-N1) | AICA-5 Authority \+ Accountability | Invisible Authority, Cascade Failure |
| Data Fragility | Perception without Signal Validation | AICA-5 Cognitive \+ ILTP | Garbage In, Garbage Out |
| Value Gap | Decision without Outcome Validation | ERDP \+ AICA-5 Ac-N3 | False Success, Repeated Failures |
| Strategic Displacement | Adaptation without Evolution System | Evolution System \+ I7 \+ I8 | Revenue Collapse, Institutional Collapse |

---

## SECTION 4: THE THREE-BRANCH GOVERNANCE ARCHITECTURE

### Branch 1: Legislative (Internal) — AICA-5

**Role:** Define what the AI is allowed/forbidden to do.

| Composition | AIGIS Instruments Controlled | Decisions They Make |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| CRO (chairs) | AICA-5 Layers 1-3 | "Credit AI can approve up to $50K; above that escalates to human." |
| CIO | ICC-8 | "Learning is authorized but must be audited quarterly." |
| CDO | CEF | "Tier 3→4 upgrade authorized; new Learning Governance Charter takes effect." |
| COO | Decision policies and authorization matrices |  |
| Domain heads |  |  |
| Strategy/Legal representative |  |  |

**They Cannot Do:** Execute AI decisions (Executive), interpret rules when ambiguous (Judicial), question whether guardrails align with external values (Ethics Board).

---

### Branch 2: Legislative (External) — Ethics Board

**Role:** Audit whether AI governance aligns with stated values; challenge legitimacy; represent stakeholder interests.

| Composition | AIGIS Instruments Monitored | Decisions They Make |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| External ethicist/philosophy expert | HOF \+ HIS-12 | "This AI system's lending decisions disproportionately exclude \[demographic\]." |
| Customer/stakeholder representative | I8 (External Legitimacy) | "Customers are losing trust. We recommend pausing Tier 4 learning." |
| Employee/labor representative | ERDP | "This Tier 5 proposal doesn't have sufficient external legitimacy." |
| Regulator/compliance expert |  |  |
| Civil society representative |  |  |

**They Cannot Do:** Write operational guardrails (AICA-5), make business decisions (Executive), interpret policy rules (Judicial).

---

### Branch 3: Executive — HAN

**Role:** Execute AI decisions within guardrails; authorize AI actions; enforce vetoes; take accountability.

| Composition | AIGIS Instruments Controlled | Decisions They Make |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| CEO (ultimate accountability) | AWOF | "Approve this AI-recommended loan." |
| CRO | ERDP | "Reject this AI-suggested strategy; it contradicts our market positioning." |
| COO | HIS-12 | "The Ethics Board raised a valid concern. We're pausing Tier 4 learning." |
| CFO | Escalation protocols |  |
| Functional heads |  |  |

**They Cannot Do:** Write new guardrails (AICA-5), interpret rules when ambiguous (Judicial), challenge external ethics concerns (Ethics Board).

---

### Branch 4: Judicial — CXOs

**Role:** Interpret what the guardrails mean; adjudicate disputes; audit ongoing compliance; issue binding interpretations.

| Composition | AIGIS Instruments Controlled | Decisions They Make |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| CRO (chairs) | AICA-5 Layers 4-5 (Observability & Meta-observability) | "This AI decision violated Guardrail B because \[reason\]." |
| CIO | Evolution System | "This guardrail is ambiguous. Our binding interpretation for future decisions is: \[interpretation\]." |
| CDO | ILTP | "The AI system is showing drift in decision character. We recommend Legislative review of constraints." |
| CCO |  |  |
| CTO |  |  |
| External auditor/ombudsman |  |  |

**They Cannot Do:** Write guardrails (AICA-5), make business decisions (Executive), challenge whether guardrails align with values (Ethics Board).

## SECTION 5: DYNAMIC ACTIVATION SCENARIOS

### Scenario 1: Normal Drift-Free Operation

**What's activated:** AICA-5 Layers 1-3, ICC-8, Observability, Judicial review (quarterly audits)

**What's not activated:** Evolution System, Escalation protocols

**Governance Posture:** Governance maintains steady state.

---

| Evolution System (triggered automatically) | Judicial: "Drift detected in \[domain\]. Recommending constraint tightening." | Observability → Evolution System → Judicial escalation → AICA-5 amendment → enforcement |
| AICA-5 special session | AICA-5: "Emergency session called. Proposed constraint amendments: \[X, Y, Z\]." |  |
| Enhanced observability (daily vs. weekly) | Executive: "Approves enhanced monitoring pending AICA-5 amendment." |  |
| CRO \+ Judicial escalation to Executive |  |  |

| Immediate rollback protocol | Executive: "Executing rollback. Pausing system pending review." |  |
| Judicial emergency investigation | Judicial: "Root cause analysis: \[guardrail was unclear / enforcement failed\]." |  |

HAWI defines the sequencing for workforce capability development aligned to governance readiness.

| Phase | Duration | Activities |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Month 1-2: Governance Readiness | 4-8 weeks | Control node owners understand their domains. Competency gaps identified. Training programs designed. |
| Month 2-3: Control Node Certification | 4 weeks | Control node owners trained on domain competencies. Authority matrices designed. Escalation policies documented. |
| Month 3-4: Workforce Training | 4 weeks | Affected roles trained on activity changes. New processes piloted. Validation protocols established. |
| Month 4-6: Pilot Deployment | 8 weeks | AI system deployed to pilot group. Workforce executes new activities. Observability infrastructure tested. |
| Month 6-12: Full Deployment | 24 weeks | AI system deployed across organization. Workforce executing at scale. Governance operating. |
| Month 12+: Evolution | Ongoing | Learning loops operating (Tier 4+). Governance evolving with AI capability. Workforce capability expanding. |

# HIS-12 v2.0 — HAN Invariants System

**Status:** Built — v2.0 (Reconciliation with HOF, HAN, and HAWI) **Type:** Human Authority Instrument **Parent Stack:** HOF (Human Operating Framework) **Version:** 2.0 — Supersedes HIS-12 v1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The HAN Invariants System (HIS-12) defines the 12 structural conditions that human authority must satisfy to be legitimate, auditable, and accountable. HIS-12 operationalizes HOF's three layers—Authority Establishment (H1–H4), Authority Execution (H5–H8), and Authority Accountability (H9–H12)—as inviolable invariants.

HIS-12 is the constitutional logic that governs HAN (Human Authority Node). HAN is the operational instantiation of HIS-12. No human authority may violate HIS-12 invariants. HIS-12 is derived from ICC-8 I1 (Accountability Invariance) and I2 (Authority-Responsibility Separation).

**The core insight:** Authority without invariants is arbitrary. Human authority must be structurally constrained, not merely procedurally guided. HIS-12 is the structural grammar of legitimate human authority.

---

## THE THREE LAYERS OF HIS-12

HIS-12 is organized into three layers, each containing four invariants:

| Layer | Invariants | Function |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Authority Establishment** | H1–H4 | Defines how authority is created, appointed, and structured |
| **Authority Execution** | H5–H8 | Defines how authority is exercised, delegated, and escalated |
| **Authority Accountability** | H9–H12 | Defines how authority is reviewed, audited, and corrected |

---

## LAYER 1: AUTHORITY ESTABLISHMENT (H1–H4)

### H1 — Single Human Authority Node Invariance

**Statement:** Authority must be vested in a single, named human. No committee, collective, or distributed consensus mechanism may substitute for a single accountability anchor.

**Violation Condition:** Authority is held by a committee, rotating position, or collective body without a single named anchor.

**Operationalization:** HAN is a single, named human appointed by the Board. HAC (Human Authority Charter) formalizes the appointment. CFL-V verifies HAN is a single named human.

**Test:** Can you name the human who holds ultimate authority? If the answer is "a committee" or "we're figuring it out," H1 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** HAN, HAC, CFL-V

---

### H2 — Board Reporting Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN reports directly to the Board. The HAN is not subordinate to the CEO, C-suite, or any operational executive. The CEO and HAN are constitutional peers.

**Violation Condition:** HAN reporting line passes through CEO, CFO, CIO, or COO.

**Operationalization:** Board Governance Cycle Integration defines HAN reporting cadence and content. HAN has direct board access. HAN may escalate to Board without operational filter.

**Test:** Does the HAN report to the CEO, or directly to the Board? If the answer is "the CEO," H2 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** Board Governance Cycle Integration, ERDP

---

### H3 — Authorization Authority Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN can affirmatively authorize and prohibit AI deployments. The HAN's authority is not limited to veto—it includes active authorization of Tier 3+ deployments.

**Violation Condition:** HAN can only veto, not authorize; or authorization authority is shared with operational executives.

**Operationalization:** A-N1 (Trigger Rights) requires HAN authorization for Tier 3+ deployments. CEF Stage 3 (Mandate Close) requires HAN confirmation. HAN's Authorization Authority is defined in the Constitutional Charter.

**Test:** Can the HAN say YES, or only NO? If the HAN can only say NO, H3 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** A-N1, CEF, Constitutional Charter

---

### H4 — Budget Independence Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN's governance budget is locked in the Board-approved charter. It cannot be reduced without Board approval. The CFO cannot unilaterally reallocate the HAN's budget.

**Violation Condition:** HAN's budget is subject to CFO reallocation or annual cost-cutting cycles without Board approval.

**Operationalization:** Budget Charter protects HAN budget from unilateral CFO reallocation. Budget Deficit State triggers Board review. ERDP includes budget disclosure.

**Test:** Can the CFO cut the HAN's budget without Board approval? If yes, H4 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** Budget Charter, ERDP

---

## LAYER 2: AUTHORITY EXECUTION (H5–H8)

### H5 — Cross-Functional Mandate Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN can direct the CIO, CFO, COO, and CXOs on governance matters. CXOs cannot override HAN's governance decisions. HAN may direct operational executives on matters of cognitive integrity, meta-observability, and constitutional compliance.

**Violation Condition:** CXOs can override HAN's governance decisions; HAN's mandate is advisory only.

**Operationalization:** HAN's Cross-Functional Mandate is defined in the Constitutional Charter. Control Node Authority Matrix maps AICA-5 nodes to decision-makers—HAN is the apex for cognitive integrity.

**Test:** Can a C-suite executive override a HAN governance directive? If yes, H5 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** Constitutional Charter, Control Node Authority Matrix

---

### H6 — No Competing Operational Authority Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN's only function is governance. The HAN does not hold operational responsibility for IT, Finance, Operations, or business execution. No conflict of interest between governance authority and operational metrics.

**Violation Condition:** HAN also runs IT, Finance, Operations, or any operational function.

**Operationalization:** HAN's job description explicitly limits scope to governance. HAN's performance metrics are governance-focused, not operational. HAN's 5 properties are verified at charter compilation.

**Test:** Does the HAN also hold an operational role? If yes, H6 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** HAN Job Description, HAN 5 Properties, CFL-V

---

### H7 — Delegation and Escalation Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN may delegate monitoring and analysis functions to AI agents under AWOF governance. The HAN may not delegate certification, suspension, or constitutional review authority. Escalation paths must be pre-defined and tested.

**Violation Condition:** HAN delegates certification or suspension authority to AI agents; escalation paths are undefined or untested.

**Operationalization:** A-N4 (Escalation Paths) defines routing of decisions and exceptions exceeding current authority levels. ADTEP Escalation Flag forces HAN review when trigger conditions are met. A-N5 (Delegation Boundaries) governs scope, duration, and revocation of delegated authority.

**Test:** Has the HAN delegated any authority that is non-delegable? Are escalation paths defined and tested? If not, H7 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** A-N4, ADTEP Escalation Flag, A-N5

---

### H8 — Override Protocol Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN retains override authority over all AI-performed institutional processes at all times. Emergency suspension capability must be present at all levels. Override mechanisms must be tested by non-technical principals.

**Violation Condition:** Override mechanisms untested; invocation requiring system-level access; override invoked by technical personnel only.

**Operationalization:** A-N3 (Override Protocols) governs conditions and mechanisms for human override. ADTEP Escalation Flag forces HAN review. A-N3 is tested by non-technical principal per governance cycle.

**Test:** Can a non-technical principal invoke the override? Has it been tested? If not, H8 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** A-N3, ADTEP Escalation Flag

---

## LAYER 3: AUTHORITY ACCOUNTABILITY (H9–H12)

### H9 — Performance Review Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN is evaluated annually by the Board against defined performance metrics. Evaluation integrates HAN self-evaluation, external audit findings, and Board assessment.

**Violation Condition:** No formal performance review; evaluation is ad-hoc or politically motivated.

**Operationalization:** Performance and Accountability Framework defines evaluation metrics, process, and timeline. HAN Scorecard System provides per-role and per-person assessment (9 dimensions \+ composite score). Governor's Reasoning Audit provides independent external validation.

**Test:** Is the HAN evaluated annually against defined metrics? If not, H9 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** Performance and Accountability Framework, HAN Scorecard System, Governor's Reasoning Audit

---

### H10 — External Review Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN's reasoning—certifications, suspensions, opinions, and findings—is audited annually by an independent external review node. The review node is structurally independent of the HAN, Board, and C-suite.

**Violation Condition:** No external audit; external audit is controlled by the HAN or Board.

**Operationalization:** Governor's Reasoning Audit is conducted by an independent external review node. Audit findings are published in Governor's Public Register. CEN-5 (Independence) requires structural separation.

**Test:** Is the HAN audited by an independent external review node? If not, H10 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** Governor's Reasoning Audit, Governor's Public Register, CEN-5

---

### H11 — Succession and Continuity Invariance

**Statement:** Succession of accountability must be defined for all critical human authority roles. Institutional function must persist through HAN unavailability, vacancy, or incapacity.

**Violation Condition:** No defined succession; institution ceases to function on HAN unavailability.

**Operationalization:** Deputy Governor and Third-Tier Succession ensure continuity. MVOS (Minimum Viable Operations State) defines HAN-only operations when AI workforce is unavailable. Reduced Operations State defined in Continuity and Succession Charter.

**Test:** Is there a defined successor for the HAN? What happens if the HAN is unavailable? If not, H11 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** Deputy Governor, Third-Tier Succession, MVOS, Continuity and Succession Charter

---

### H12 — Removal and Due Process Invariance

**Statement:** The HAN may be removed only by Board supermajority vote, after independent investigation and due process. Removal is not arbitrary or politically motivated.

**Violation Condition:** HAN removed by simple majority; removal without investigation; removal for political reasons.

**Operationalization:** Removal requires supermajority vote (two-thirds or more). Independent investigation by external review node precedes removal. Grounds for removal are defined (material negligence, misrepresentation, constitutional violation, incapacity, conflict of interest).

**Test:** Can the HAN be removed arbitrarily? Is there a defined process with due process? If not, H12 is violated.

**AIGIS Component:** Performance and Accountability Framework, Governor's Reasoning Audit

---

## SUMMARY TABLE

| Layer | Invariant | Core Requirement | Violation Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Authority Establishment** | H1 — Single Human Authority Node | Authority vested in a single named human | Authority held by committee or collective |
|  | H2 — Board Reporting | HAN reports directly to Board | HAN reports through CEO/C-suite |
|  | H3 — Authorization Authority | HAN can say YES and NO | HAN can only veto |
|  | H4 — Budget Independence | HAN budget locked by Board | CFO can reallocate budget |
| **Authority Execution** | H5 — Cross-Functional Mandate | HAN can direct CXOs on governance | HAN mandate is advisory only |
|  | H6 — No Competing Operational Authority | HAN only governance | HAN also holds operational role |
|  | H7 — Delegation and Escalation | Non-delegable authority retained; escalation defined | HAN delegates certification; escalation undefined |
|  | H8 — Override Protocol | Override exists and is tested | Override untested or unreachable |
| **Authority Accountability** | H9 — Performance Review | HAN evaluated annually against metrics | No formal performance review |
|  | H10 — External Review | HAN audited by independent external node | No external audit or node not independent |
|  | H11 — Succession and Continuity | Succession defined; function persists | No defined succession |
|  | H12 — Removal and Due Process | Removal by supermajority after investigation | Removal arbitrary or without due process |

---

## CFL-V VALIDATION RULES

For any human authority structure, CFL-V must verify:

**H1:** Authority is vested in a single named human (HAN)  
**H2:** HAN reports directly to Board  
**H3:** HAN has Authorization Authority (can say YES and NO)  
**H4:** HAN budget is protected from CFO reallocation  
**H5:** HAN has Cross-Functional Mandate over CXOs on governance  
**H6:** HAN has no competing operational authority  
**H7:** Non-delegable authorities are retained; escalation paths are defined  
**H8:** Override mechanisms exist and are tested by non-technical principals  
**H9:** HAN is evaluated annually against defined metrics  
**H10:** HAN is audited by an independent external review node  
**H11:** Succession is defined; function persists through HAN unavailability  
**H12:** Removal requires supermajority after independent investigation

**No human authority passes CFL-V without satisfying all 12 invariants.**
