## SECTION 5: CANDIDATE CONTESTATION PROTOCOL

### Purpose

Candidates may contest examination results or portfolio adjudication findings through a defined due process protocol.

### Protocol Steps

| Step | Action | Responsible | Timeline |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Contest submission | Candidate | Within 14 days of result notification |
| 2 | Contest specifies grounds for dispute with supporting evidence | Candidate | Within 14 days of result notification |
| 3 | Independent review: F-OV agent from non-Institute entity conducts review of examination marking or portfolio adjudication against curriculum standards | F-OV Agent (cross-review) | Within 14 days of contest submission |
| 4 | HAN makes final determination based on independent review finding | HAN | Within 7 days of independent review |
| 5 | Candidate receives the finding and HAN determination | 19 Institute | Within 3 days of HAN determination |
| 6 | Review is logged as an audit artifact under I3 of ICC-8 | IMP | Upon completion |

### Contestation Rules

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Due Process** | Candidates have the right to contest examination results or portfolio adjudication findings. |
| **Independent Review** | Review is conducted by an F-OV agent from a non-Institute entity (cross-review under AWOF v1.1 Section 12). |
| **HAN Final Determination** | HAN makes the final determination based on the independent review finding. |
| **IMP Logging** | Review is logged as an audit artifact under I3 of ICC-8. |
| **Finality** | HAN determination is final. |

---

## SECTION 6: PUBLIC DESIGNATION REGISTER

### Purpose

The Public Designation Register is the external legibility instrument of the certification function under I8 of ICC-8. It is a canonical list of all designation holders with current status.

### Status Classifications

| Status | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Active** | Designation is current and in good standing |
| **Under Revalidation** | Designation holder is within a revalidation window or approved extension period |
| **Proceeding Suspended** | Revocation proceeding is active but suspended due to HAN unavailability |
| **Lapsed** | Periodic renewal not completed within required window |
| **Revoked** | Designation permanently withdrawn by HAN determination |

### Register Contents

| Field | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Candidate Name** | Full name of designation holder |
| **Designation Post-Nominal** | CA / CI / CGO / etc. |
| **Award Date** | Date of designation award |
| **Current Status** | Active / Under Revalidation / Proceeding Suspended / Lapsed / Revoked |
| **Last Renewal or Revalidation Date** | Date of most recent renewal or revalidation |

### Confidentiality

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Public Information** | Public Designation Register contains: candidate name, designation post-nominal, award date, current status, last renewal/revalidation date. |
| **Confidential Information** | Public Designation Register does not contain: examination scores, portfolio content, contestation records, or other confidential information. |
| **Confidential Storage** | Confidential information is held in the Candidate Record under I6 restricted classification. |

### Verification

| Party | Verification Purpose |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Employers** | Verify designation status of employees or applicants |
| **DFIs** | Verify designation status of practitioners |
| **Regulatory Bodies** | Verify designation status for regulatory compliance |
| **Public** | Verify designation status of any holder |

### Misrepresentation

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Lapsed or Revoked Representation** | Misrepresentation of a Lapsed or Revoked designation as Active is a violation of 19 Institute designation holder conduct standards. |
| **Enforcement** | Misrepresentation is referred to the HoldCo contestation interface under CEN-2 of ICC-8. |
| **Revocation Ground** | Misrepresentation is grounds for revocation proceeding. |

---

## SECTION 7: DESIGNATION MAINTENANCE

### 7.1 Periodic Renewal

| Aspect | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Cycle** | 2 years from award date, then 2 years from each prior renewal date |
| **Renewal Requirement** | Completion of a defined continuing education requirement specified in program curriculum, or demonstration of active framework deployment in professional practice |
| **IMP Logging** | Renewal is logged in Candidate Record and Public Designation Register updated |
| **Failure to Complete** | Failure to complete renewal within the 2-year window: designation status changes to Lapsed |

### Lapse and Reinstatement

| Aspect | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Lapse** | Designation status changes to Lapsed upon failure to complete renewal within the 2-year window |
| **Reinstatement (within 12 months)** | Lapsed designations may be reinstated within 12 months of lapse date by completing renewal requirements plus a reinstatement assessment defined in program curriculum |
| **Reinstatement (beyond 12 months)** | Reinstatement beyond 12 months requires full reassessment under current program curriculum |
| **IMP Logging** | Reinstatement is logged in Candidate Record and Public Designation Register updated |

### 7.2 Event-Triggered Revalidation

| Aspect | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Trigger** | Material change to the governing framework version bound to the designation curriculum (Curriculum Review Protocol under ILTP v2.0 Section 8.2) |
| **Trigger Determination** | HAN determination under Curriculum Review Protocol that the framework version change is material and requires revalidation |
| **Revalidation Window** | Defined per trigger event, minimum 90 days from notification |
| **Revalidation Requirement** | Defined per trigger event in Curriculum Review Protocol finding — may be targeted assessment, portfolio supplement, or full reassessment depending on materiality of change |
| **Designation Status** | Designation status during revalidation window: Under Revalidation |

### Revalidation Extension Protocol

| Aspect | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Extension Request** | Candidates may request extension with documented cause |
| **Extension Authorization** | Extension is HAN-authorized |
| **Maximum Extension** | 90 additional days |
| **Designation Status** | Designation status remains Under Revalidation during extension |
| **Suspension** | Designation is not suspended during extension period |

### Revalidation Failure

| Aspect | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Failure to Complete** | Failure to complete revalidation within window plus any authorized extension: designation status changes to Lapsed under standard Lapse provisions |
| **IMP Logging** | Revalidation failure is logged in Candidate Record and Public Designation Register updated |

---

## SECTION 8: REVOCATION

### Purpose

Designation revocation is the permanent withdrawal of a designation by HAN determination.

### Revocation Grounds

| \# | Ground | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **RG-1** | **Candidate Attestation Violation** | Undisclosed AI generation producing submission substantially indistinguishable from another candidate's submission |
| **RG-2** | **Material Misrepresentation** | Material misrepresentation in portfolio submission or examination |
| **RG-3** | **Code of Conduct Violation** | Breach of 19 Institute designation holder conduct standards (defined in program curriculum) |
| **RG-4** | **Status Misrepresentation** | Material misrepresentation of designation status to external counterparties |
| **RG-5** | **Constitutional Integrity** | HAN determination that continued designation holding is inconsistent with the integrity of the certification function |
| **RG-6** | **I9 Catastrophic Risk Violation** | Designation holder's actions violate I9 Catastrophic Risk Invariant (v2.0) |

### Revocation Proceeding

| Step | Action | Responsible | Timeline |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Revocation proceeding initiated by HAN or by complaint received through HoldCo contestation interface | HAN / Complainant | Upon detection |
| 2 | Candidate notified of proceeding initiation and grounds | 19 Institute | Within 7 days |
| 3 | Candidate has 21 days to submit a response | Candidate | Within 21 days |
| 4 | HAN reviews grounds and candidate response | HAN | Within 30 days of response |
| 5 | HAN issues determination: revocation confirmed or proceeding closed | HAN | Within 30 days of response |
| 6 | Revocation is logged in Candidate Record and Public Designation Register updated to Revoked status | IMP | Upon determination |

### HAN Unavailability During Revocation Proceeding

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Proceeding Suspended** | Proceeding is suspended. |
| **Designation Status** | Designation status is updated to Proceeding Suspended in the Public Designation Register. |
| **Resumption** | Proceeding resumes upon HAN restoration. |

### Revocation Consequences

| Consequence | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Permanent** | Revocation is permanent. |
| **Fresh Assessment** | Revoked designation holders may apply for fresh assessment under current program curriculum after a minimum 2-year period from revocation date, at HAN discretion. |
| **Public Designation Register** | Status remains Revoked permanently. |

---

## SECTION 9: FELLOWSHIP DESIGNATION

### Purpose

The 19 Integrated Fellow (FI19) designation is a distinct class governed by special rules.

### Governance

| Aspect | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Assessment Model** | No fixed assessment model — HAN-adjudicated based on demonstrated contribution to 19 Integrated framework development, institutional adoption, or thought leadership |
| **Periodic Renewal** | No periodic renewal requirement — Fellowship is permanent once awarded unless revoked |
| **Event-Triggered Revalidation** | Subject to event-triggered revalidation only if HAN determines that a material framework change affects the basis of the original award |
| **Nomination** | Fellowship award requires HAN nomination and confirmation — no candidate application process |
| **Public Designation Register** | Fellowship is listed in the Public Designation Register as a distinct designation class |

### Revocation

| Aspect | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Grounds** | Same as Section 8 (RG-1 through RG-6) |
| **Proceeding** | Same as Section 8 |
| **Consequences** | Same as Section 8 |

# Public Designation Register v2.0

**Status:** Built — v2.0 (Reconciliation with CGF, ICC-8, ERDP, IMP, and HAN/HOF)  
**Type:** Certification Governance Instrument  
**Parent Stack:** CGF (Certification Governance Framework)  
**Version:** 2.0 — Supersedes Public Designation Register v1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The Public Designation Register is the external legibility instrument of the certification function under I8 of ICC-8. It answers: *Who holds a 19 Institute designation, what is their current status, and how can external parties verify that status?*

The Public Designation Register is a canonical list of all designation holders with their current status. It provides external legibility of certification status—satisfying I8 External Legibility requirement by making the certification function auditable, verifiable, and contestable from outside the institution.

**The core insight:** A certification that cannot be verified externally is not a certification—it is a claim. The Public Designation Register transforms certification from an institutional assertion into an externally verifiable fact, enabling employers, regulators, DFIs, and the public to trust the designation.

---

## SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND SCOPE

### Purpose

The Public Designation Register ensures that:

1. **Designation status is externally verifiable** — Employers, regulators, DFIs, and the public can verify status  
2. **Status is current** — The Register reflects real-time status changes (Active, Under Revalidation, Lapsed, Revoked, Proceeding Suspended)  
3. **Confidentiality is maintained** — The Register contains only public information; confidential records remain restricted  
4. **I8 External Legibility is satisfied** — The certification function is externally legible, auditable, and contestable  
5. **Misrepresentation is detectable** — Lapsed or Revoked designations are visible to prevent misrepresentation

### Scope

| In Scope | Out of Scope |
| :---- | :---- |
| Designation holder names and post-nominals | Examination scores |
| Current status classifications | Portfolio content |
| Award and renewal dates | Contestation records |
| Verification by external parties | Candidate contact information |
| External legibility under I8 | Confidential candidate records |

### Governing Relationships

| Instrument | Relationship to Public Designation Register |
| :---- | :---- |
| **CGF** | Parent instrument — Public Designation Register is a component of CGF |
| **ICC-8** | Constitutional parent — I8 External Legibility requirement |
| **ERDP** | Disclosure and reporting — Register status feeds ERDP |
| **IMP** | Certification records logged as GAO, DRO, OEO |
| **HAN/HOF** | Status changes require HAN authorization |

---

## SECTION 2: REGISTER STRUCTURE

### 2.1 Register Schema

| \# | Field | Type | Description | Publicly Visible |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | **Registration ID** | String | Unique identifier. Format: `PDR-[SEQ]` | No |
| 2 | **Candidate Name** | String | Full name of the designation holder | Yes |
| 3 | **Designation Post-Nominal** | String | CA / CI / CGO / MCP / MCA / CCO / FI19 | Yes |
| 4 | **Designation Class** | Enum | Practitioner — Foundation / Practitioner — Applied / Practitioner — Senior / Specialist / Fellowship | Yes |
| 5 | **Award Date** | ISO 8601 | Date of designation award | Yes |
| 6 | **Current Status** | Enum | Active / Under Revalidation / Proceeding Suspended / Lapsed / Revoked | Yes |
| 7 | **Last Renewal or Revalidation Date** | ISO 8601 | Date of most recent renewal or revalidation | Yes |
| 8 | **Next Renewal Due Date** | ISO 8601 | Date by which next renewal is due | Yes |
| 9 | **Governing Framework Version** | String | IP-FD version bound at program launch | Yes |
| 10 | **Status Change History** | Array | Log of all status changes with timestamps | No (audit only) |
| 11 | **HAN Acknowledgment** | Object | HAN signature and date for each status change | No (audit only) |
| 12 | **Verification Count** | Integer | Number of external verification requests | No (internal metric) |

### 2.2 Status Classifications

| Status | Meaning | Public Display | Transition To |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Active** | Designation is current and in good standing | ✅ Active | Under Revalidation, Lapsed, Revoked |
| **Under Revalidation** | Designation holder is within a revalidation window or approved extension period | ⚠️ Under Revalidation | Active, Lapsed, Revoked |
| **Proceeding Suspended** | Revocation proceeding is active but suspended due to HAN unavailability | ⏸️ Proceeding Suspended | Active, Revoked |
| **Lapsed** | Periodic renewal not completed within required window | ❌ Lapsed | Active (reinstatement within 12 months), Revoked |
| **Revoked** | Designation permanently withdrawn by HAN determination | ❌ Revoked | — (terminal state) |

### 2.3 Status Display Rules

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Active** | Displayed as "Active" with green indicator |
| **Under Revalidation** | Displayed as "Under Revalidation" with yellow indicator; shows revalidation window end date if applicable |
| **Proceeding Suspended** | Displayed as "Proceeding Suspended" with orange indicator; shows suspension reason (HAN unavailable) |
| **Lapsed** | Displayed as "Lapsed" with red indicator; shows lapse date |
| **Revoked** | Displayed as "Revoked" with red indicator; shows revocation date; permanent |

## SECTION 3: REGISTER MAINTENANCE

### 3.1 Status Update Triggers

| Trigger | New Status | Responsible | Timeline |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Designation awarded | Active | 19 Institute | Upon HAN confirmation |
| Renewal completed | Active | 19 Institute | Upon renewal confirmation |
| Renewal not completed within window | Lapsed | 19 Institute | Immediately upon window expiration |
| Revalidation triggered | Under Revalidation | 19 Institute | Upon trigger determination |
| Revalidation completed | Active | 19 Institute | Upon revalidation confirmation |
| Revalidation not completed within window | Lapsed | 19 Institute | Immediately upon window expiration |
| Revalidation extension granted | Under Revalidation | 19 Institute | Upon HAN authorization |
| Revocation proceeding initiated | Active (with flag) | 19 Institute | Upon HAN initiation |
| Revocation confirmed | Revoked | 19 Institute | Upon HAN determination |
| Proceeding suspended (HAN unavailable) | Proceeding Suspended | 19 Institute | Upon HAN unavailability |
| Proceeding resumed | Active (with flag) | 19 Institute | Upon HAN restoration |
| Lapsed reinstatement within 12 months | Active | 19 Institute | Upon reinstatement completion |
| Lapsed reinstatement beyond 12 months | Requires full reassessment | 19 Institute | Upon program re-entry |

### 3.2 Status Update Authorization

| Action | Authorization Required | Authorization Type |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Active → Under Revalidation | HAN | Non-delegable |
| Under Revalidation → Active | HAN | Non-delegable |
| Under Revalidation → Lapsed | Automatic | System |
| Active → Lapsed | Automatic | System |
| Lapsed → Active (reinstatement) | HAN | Non-delegable |
| Any status → Revoked | HAN | Non-delegable |
| Active → Proceeding Suspended | Automatic | System (HAN unavailability) |
| Proceeding Suspended → Active | HAN | Non-delegable |

### 3.3 Status Change Rules

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Immediate Update** | Status changes are reflected in the Register immediately upon trigger. |
| **HAN Authorization** | Status changes requiring HAN authorization are held pending HAN confirmation. |
| **Audit Trail** | All status changes are logged with timestamp, authorizer, and basis. |
| **No Retroactive Changes** | Status changes are not retroactive. The Register reflects current status at all times. |
| **Public Notification** | Status changes affecting public display are reflected immediately. |

| **Public Notification** | Notification of revocation due to misrepresentation | 19 Institute |
| **Legal Action** | Legal action for fraudulent misrepresentation | 19 Integrated Legal |

## SECTION 7: REGISTER AND ICC-8

### 7.1 I8 External Legibility

The Public Designation Register satisfies I8 External Legibility by providing:

| Requirement | How It Is Satisfied |
| :---- | :---- |
| **CEN-1: Interpretability** | Register entries are described in plain language, intelligible to external parties |
| **CEN-2: Accessibility** | Public web interface and API provide defined pathways for verification |
| **CEN-3: Traceability** | Register entries connect to audit chain under I3 |
| **CEN-4: Confidentiality** | Confidential information is not disclosed; restricted information handled by independent review |
| **CEN-5: Independence** | Register is administered by 19 Institute, not the originating authority (HAN) |
| **CEN-6: Redress and Remediation** | Misrepresentation is a revocation ground with defined corrective pathway |

### 7.2 Register and I6 Transparency Gradient

| Disclosure Tier | Content | Publicly Visible |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **T-PB (Public)** | Candidate name, designation post-nominal, current status, award date, last renewal date, governing framework version | Yes |
| **T-SH (Stakeholder)** | Verification history, renewal history | No (available to designation holder) |
| **T-RG (Regulator)** | Full Candidate Record upon lawful request | No |
| **T-DS (DFI/Sovereign)** | Full Candidate Record upon lawful request | No |

# ERDP v2.0 — External Reporting & Disclosure Protocol

**Status:** Built — v2.0 (Reconciliation with ICC-8, CEN-1 to CEN-7, IMP, AICA-5, ILTP, CGF, HAN/HOF, and DEP)  
**Type:** Reporting & Disclosure Instrument  
**Parent Stack:** 19 Integrated Operational Infrastructure  
**Version:** 2.0 — Supersedes ERDP v1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The External Reporting & Disclosure Protocol (ERDP) governs all external reporting and disclosure obligations of 19 Integrated and its three SPV entities. It answers: *What is disclosed, to whom, on what schedule, and under what conditions?*

ERDP operationalizes the external legibility requirement under I8 of ICC-8 and the Contestation Interface Standard (CEN-1 through CEN-7) across all entities. It defines what is disclosed, to whom, on what schedule, and under what conditions. It ensures that 19 Integrated's institutional actions are externally legible, auditable, and contestable.

**The core insight:** A governance structure that cannot be seen from outside is not governance—it is a private arrangement. ERDP transforms institutional governance from an internal practice into an externally verifiable system, satisfying the constitutional requirement that all material institutional actions be mappable to an external interpretation path.

---

## SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND SCOPE

### Purpose

ERDP ensures that:

1. **External legibility is maintained** — I8 External Legibility is operationalized through defined disclosure  
2. **Disclosure is tiered** — Four disclosure tiers define what is disclosed to whom  
3. **Reporting is periodic** — Annual Institutional Report (AIR) and Quarterly Operational Update (QOU) provide regular disclosure  
4. **Event-triggered reporting is defined** — Material events trigger disclosure within defined windows  
5. **Confidentiality is protected** — I6 Transparency Gradient is respected  
6. **Contestation is enabled** — CEN-1 to CEN-7 provide external contestation pathways

### Scope

| In Scope | Out of Scope |
| :---- | :---- |
| External reporting and disclosure obligations | Client engagement confidentiality (CEF) |
| Four disclosure tiers (T-PB, T-SH, T-RG, T-DS) | IP licensing terms (ILTP) |
| Annual Institutional Report (AIR) | Business strategy or marketing |
| Quarterly Operational Update (QOU) | Operational efficiency |
| Event-triggered reporting | Technical delivery execution |
| Contestation interface (CEN-1 to CEN-7) | Internal operational reporting |

### Governing Relationships

| Instrument | Relationship to ERDP |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ICC-8** | Constitutional parent — I6 Transparency Gradient, I8 External Legibility |
| **CEN-1 to CEN-7** | Contestation Interface Standard — ERDP operationalizes CEN requirements |
| **IMP** | Disclosure Records logged as GAO, DRO, OEO, XOO |
| **AICA-5** | Measurement Framework feeds ERDP reporting |
| **ILTP** | IP Register status feeds ERDP reporting |
| **CGF** | Public Designation Register feeds ERDP reporting |
| **HAN/HOF** | HAN authorizes disclosures |
| **DEP** | ERDP amendments require DEP process |

## SECTION 2: DISCLOSURE TIERS

| Tier | Code | Audience | Content Scope | Examples |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Public** | T-PB | General public, open access | Institutional existence, framework doctrine layer, designation register status, annual summary | Framework names, designation register, institutional structure |
| **Stakeholder** | T-SH | Designation holders, engagement counterparties, ecosystem contacts | Operational updates, framework version changes, certification program updates, engagement-relevant disclosures | Framework version changes, program updates, engagement-relevant disclosures |
| **Regulator** | T-RG | Philippine regulatory bodies, operating jurisdiction regulators | Governance structure, accountability architecture, compliance-relevant institutional actions | Governance structure, HAN identification, compliance actions |
| **DFI/Sovereign** | T-DS | ADB, IFC, AIIB, sovereign bodies, ASEAN regulatory counterparties | Full institutional governance package, framework stack architecture, certification standing, financial structure summary | Full governance package, framework stack, certification standing |

### Tier Assignment Rules

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Tier Assignment at Preparation** | Every disclosure item carries a tier assignment at the point of preparation. |
| **Disclosure Depth Standard** | T-PB: Doctrine-layer information only; T-SH: Operational updates; T-RG: Governance structure; T-DS: Full governance package. |
| **Tier Elevation** | Reclassification to a higher tier requires HAN authorization. |
| **No Down-Tiering** | Information may be elevated to a higher tier but may not be down-tiered without HAN authorization. |

### Disclosure Depth Standard

| Tier | Content Scope | Prohibited Content |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **T-PB** | Institutional existence, framework doctrine layer, designation register status, annual summary | Operational specifications, invariant formalism, implementation logic, assessment criteria, client-specific information |
| **T-SH** | Operational updates, framework version changes, certification program updates, engagement-relevant disclosures | Internal operational data, financial structure detail, client-specific information |
| **T-RG** | Governance structure, accountability architecture, compliance-relevant institutional actions | Internal operational data, client-specific information |
| **T-DS** | Full institutional governance package, framework stack architecture, certification standing, financial structure summary | Board deliberation content, privileged communications, client-specific information |

## SECTION 5: SPECIAL DISCLOSURE PROTOCOLS

### 5.1 Contestation Disclosure Rule

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Under Contestation Review** | Any material action under active contestation at the time of reporting is disclosed as Under Contestation Review. |
| **Action Description** | The nature of the action is described; findings are withheld pending resolution. |
| **Post-Resolution** | Post-resolution outcome is carried in the subsequent reporting period or as an event-triggered disclosure within 30 days of resolution. |
| **CEN-7 Public Contestation** | Public contestation submissions are disclosed in aggregate (no individual identification). |

### 5.2 Tier Elevation Protocol

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Request** | A DFI, regulatory, or sovereign counterparty may request access to a classification tier above their standard entitlement. |
| **Formal Instrument** | Request must specify scope, purpose, and duration of elevated access. |
| **Authorization** | Tier elevation requires HAN authorization. |
| **No Reclassification** | Elevated access does not reclassify the underlying information. |
| **Reversion** | Access reverts to standard tier upon expiry. |
| **IMP Logging** | Tier elevation instruments are logged as audit artifacts under I3. |

### 5.3 Emergency Disclosure Protocol

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Trigger** | HAN unavailable and mandatory event-triggered disclosure window at risk of expiry. |
| **Action** | Disclosure is filed as Pending HAN Authorization with event description, timestamp, and unavailability notation. |
| **Timing** | This satisfies the timing requirement. |
| **Full Disclosure** | Full disclosure is completed upon HAN restoration. |
| **IMP Logging** | The Pending filing is logged as an audit artifact under I3. |
| **I9 Emergency Disclosure** | I9 violations require immediate disclosure regardless of HAN availability. |

### 5.4 Post-Publication Correction Protocol

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Trigger** | Material error discovered after publication. |
| **Action** | Correction Notice issued to all audiences that received the original report. |
| **Correction Content** | Correction clearly identified and dated. |
| **IMP Logging** | Correction Notice is logged as an audit artifact. |
| **Archival** | Original report is archived in the IP Register with a correction flag. |
| **DFI/Sovereign Notification** | Corrections to T-DS disclosures require direct counterparty notification. |

### 5.5 Jurisdictional Scope Rule

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Mandatory Disclosure** | Mandatory disclosure obligations apply within 19 Integrated's defined operating jurisdictions. |
| **Extra-Jurisdictional Requests** | Extra-jurisdictional regulatory requests are treated as voluntary disclosure requests. |
| **Handling** | Handled through the Tier Elevation Protocol. |
| **HAN Determination** | HAN determines whether voluntary disclosure serves institutional interests. |
| **No Mandatory Obligation** | No mandatory disclosure obligation exists outside defined operating jurisdictions. |

### 5.6 Data Reconciliation Rule

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Reference Date** | All quantitative disclosures referencing data maintained in other instruments carry a reference date. |
| **Governing Figure** | The reference date governs the figure disclosed. |
| **Discrepancy Resolution** | Discrepancies between a report figure and a live register are resolved by reference to the stated reference date. |
| **Instrument Sources** | Public Designation Register, IP Register, Engagement Records |

### 5.7 I9 Catastrophic Risk Disclosure Protocol

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Immediate Disclosure** | I9 violations trigger immediate event-triggered disclosure. |
| **Timeline** | Disclosure within 24 hours of violation. |
| **Audience** | T-RG and T-DS tiers; T-SH notification. |
| **Content** | Nature of violation, containment status, HAN escalation, system shutdown status (if applicable). |
| **Follow-Up** | Post-incident review disclosure within 60 days. |
| **No Delay for HAN Unavailability** | Emergency Disclosure Protocol applies immediately. |

## SECTION 9: ERDP AND CEN-1 TO CEN-7

| CEN | Requirement | ERDP Implementation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **CEN-1: Interpretability** | Actions describable to external parties without internal access | AIR and QOU use plain language; external interpretation path maintained |
| **CEN-2: Accessibility** | Defined pathway for external parties to raise objections | Contestation Disclosure Rule; Tier Elevation Protocol; Public Designation Register |
| **CEN-3: Traceability** | Connects to audit chain; contestation triggers reconstructability review | Disclosure Records logged in IMP; traceable to I3 audit chain |
| **CEN-4: Confidentiality** | Restricted information handled by independent review node | T-RG and T-DS tiers; I6 confidentiality protections |
| **CEN-5: Independence** | Originating authority cannot hold voting/blocking rights in contestation | HAN authorizes but does not control independent review |
| **CEN-6: Redress and Remediation** | Corrective actions require I7 continuity impact assessment | Post-Publication Correction Protocol; Correction Notice |
| **CEN-7: Public Contestation** | Any individual may submit a governance concern | Public contestation logged as OEO; 30-day response window; HAN escalation |

# AIR v2.0 — Annual Institutional Report

**Status:** Built — v2.0 (Reconciliation with ERDP, ICC-8, IMP, AICA-5, ILTP, CGF, HAN/HOF, and DEP)  
**Type:** Reporting & Disclosure Instrument  
**Parent Stack:** ERDP (External Reporting & Disclosure Protocol)  
**Version:** 2.0 — Supersedes AIR v1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The Annual Institutional Report (AIR) is the primary periodic disclosure instrument of 19 Integrated, providing external legibility of governance health under ICC-8 I8 External Legibility Invariance. It answers: *What is the state of 19 Integrated's governance architecture, and what material actions have occurred during the reporting period?*

AIR provides periodic external disclosure of governance health—satisfying the periodic disclosure cycle requirement of CEN-4 and the external legibility interface required under I8. It ensures that 19 Integrated's institutional actions are externally legible, auditable, and contestable from outside the institution.

**The core insight:** A governance structure that is never externally reported is not transparent—it is private. AIR transforms internal governance into externally verifiable institutional fact, satisfying the constitutional requirement that material institutional actions be periodically disclosed to defined external parties.

---

## SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND SCOPE

### Purpose

AIR ensures that:

1. **Governance health is externally legible** — External parties can assess governance health  
2. **Material actions are disclosed** — Material institutional actions are reported  
3. **Periodic disclosure is maintained** — Annual cadence satisfies CEN-4  
4. **Transparency is tiered** — Tier-specific versions serve different audiences  
5. **Accountability is demonstrated** — HAN attests to report accuracy  
6. **Contestation is enabled** — AIR provides basis for external contestation

### Scope

| In Scope | Out of Scope |
| :---- | :---- |
| Annual governance health disclosure | Client engagement confidentiality (CEF) |
| Tier-specific versions (T-PB, T-SH, T-RG, T-DS) | IP licensing terms (ILTP) |
| Seven sections of AIR content | Business strategy or marketing |
| HAN attestation | Operational efficiency |
| Disclosure Record logging | Technical delivery execution |

### Governing Relationships

| Instrument | Relationship to AIR |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ERDP** | Parent instrument — AIR is the primary periodic report of ERDP |
| **ICC-8** | Constitutional parent — I8 External Legibility, I6 Transparency Gradient |
| **CEN-4** | Periodic disclosure cycle — AIR satisfies CEN-4 |
| **IMP** | AIR logged as GAO; Disclosure Record logged |
| **AICA-5** | Measurement Framework feeds AIR |
| **ILTP** | IP Register status feeds AIR |
| **CGF** | Public Designation Register feeds AIR |
| **HAN/HOF** | HAN attests to report accuracy |

## SECTION 3: AIR CONTENT — SECTION 1: INSTITUTIONAL IDENTITY

### Purpose

Provides external parties with the foundational identity and governance structure of 19 Integrated.

### Content

| \# | Field | Description | Tier |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | **HoldCo Structure** | Description of 19 Integrated HoldCo and its role | All |
| 2 | **SPV Federation** | Description of 19 Consultin', 19 Publishin', 19 Institute | All |
| 3 | **HAN Identification** | Human Authority Node name and role | All |
| 4 | **Constitutional Stack Reference** | ICC-8 v2.0 reference and compliance statement | All |

## The One-Sentence Summary

> *"AIR v2.0 is the Annual Institutional Report — a 7-section periodic disclosure instrument (Institutional Identity, Framework Stack Status, Certification Activity, Engagement Activity Summary, Governance Events, Regulatory Correspondence, Forward Governance) produced in tier-specific versions (T-PB, T-SH, T-RG, T-DS), attested by HAN under penalty of Ac-N2 violation, and logged in IMP as a GAO, satisfying I8 External Legibility and CEN-4 periodic disclosure under ERDP and ICC-8 constitutional governance."*


# Stack Version Map v2.0

**Status:** Built — v2.0 (Reconciliation with DEP, IMP, ICC-8, and all stack instruments)  
**Type:** Meta-Governance Instrument  
**Parent Stack:** DEP (Doctrine Extension Protocol)  
**Version:** 2.0 — Supersedes Stack Version Map v1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The Stack Version Map is a living record maintained in IMP of the current canonical version of every instrument in the 19 Integrated governance stack. It answers: *What is the current version of every instrument, and what was the last change made to each?*

The Stack Version Map is updated upon every authorized DEP change. It is the reference document for governance version binding on all new IMP objects. Historical objects are read against the framework version that governed them—the Map preserves the version history so that objects created under prior versions remain auditable and interpretable.

**The core insight:** Versioning is governance. Without a version map, an institution cannot know what rules applied when. The Stack Version Map makes governance version binding real—ensuring that every institutional object carries the version of the framework that governed its creation.

---

## SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND SCOPE

### Purpose

The Stack Version Map ensures that:

1. **Current versions are known** — Every instrument has a declared current version  
2. **Version history is preserved** — Historical versions remain accessible for audit  
3. **DEP changes are tracked** — Every DEP change updates the Map  
4. **Version binding is maintained** — Objects reference the version active at creation  
5. **Instrument relationships are visible** — Dependencies between instruments are documented  
6. **Layer classification is maintained** — Each instrument is classified by layer

### Scope

| In Scope | Out of Scope |
| :---- | :---- |
| All canonical stack instruments | Client engagement deliverables |
| Version numbers and history | Business strategy or marketing |
| DEP change tracking | Operational efficiency |
| Layer classification | Technical delivery execution |
| Instrument dependencies | Commercial decisions |

### Governing Relationships

| Instrument | Relationship to Stack Version Map |
| :---- | :---- |
| **DEP** | Parent instrument — Map updated upon every DEP change |
| **IMP** | Map stored as GAO; version binding referenced by all IMP objects |
| **ICC-8** | Constitutional ceiling — Map reflects ICC-8 versions |
| **All stack instruments** | Map records current version of each |

## SECTION 4: VERSION BINDING

### Purpose

Governance version binding ensures that every institutional object is bound to the version of the governing framework active at the time of its creation. Subsequent framework updates do not retroactively alter historical objects.

### Implementation

| Field | Source | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **governing\_framework\_versions** | ECO, DRO, GAO, CRO, OEO, XOO | Key-value map of framework ID to version string active at object creation |
| **version\_binding\_timestamp** | All IMP objects | Timestamp of version binding |
| **stack\_version\_map\_reference** | All IMP objects | Reference to Stack Version Map version at creation |

### Binding Rules

| Rule | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Creation Binding** | Objects are bound to the version active at creation |
| **Immutable** | Version binding is immutable; subsequent updates do not alter historical objects |
| **Audit Access** | Historical objects are read against the framework version that governed them |
| **Map Reference** | Stack Version Map version is referenced in each object |

### Binding Example

Object: GAO-ECO-2026-0a26cb-001  
governing\_framework\_versions:  
  ICC-8: "v2.0"  
  AICA-5: "v2.0"  
  AWOF: "v2.0"  
  IMP: "v2.0"  
version\_binding\_timestamp: "2026-08-31T10:00:00Z"  
stack\_version\_map\_reference: "SVM-2026-08-31"

# DEP v2.0 — Doctrine Extension Protocol

**Status:** Built — v2.0 (Reconciliation with ICC-8, IMP, AICA-5, AWOF, EAF, ILTP, CGF, ERDP, HAN/HOF, and all other stack instruments)  
**Type:** Meta-Governance Instrument  
**Parent Stack:** 19 Integrated Meta-Governance Layer  
**Version:** 2.0 — Supersedes DEP v1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The Doctrine Extension Protocol (DEP) is the meta-governance instrument of 19 Integrated. It governs how the institutional framework stack — IMP, EAF, ICC-8, AICA-5, AWOF, ILTP, CGF, ERDP, RGI-8, CAD-7, and all instruments derived from them — may be extended, amended, superseded, or retired. It answers: *By what governed process does the institution's own doctrine evolve without drifting?*

DEP is not an amendment procedure, a version control policy, or a change management checklist. It is the **constitutional amendment logic** of 19 Integrated. Without DEP, the framework stack is a closed system that cannot adapt. With an ungoverned extension process, the stack becomes arbitrary — frameworks proliferate without constitutional grounding, instruments contradict each other, and the compounding institutional intelligence that IMP is designed to build degrades into noise.

**The core insight:** A governance stack that cannot evolve is brittle; a governance stack that evolves without governance is chaotic. DEP resolves this by establishing what qualifies as a valid doctrine extension signal, how signals are evaluated, what classes of change are permitted, who may authorize each class, and how the record of doctrine evolution is maintained.

---

## SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND SCOPE

### Purpose

DEP ensures that:

1. **Doctrine evolves from evidence** — Extensions trace to documented signals, not preference or convenience  
2. **The stack remains constitutional** — Changes preserve ICC-8 invariants  
3. **Change is minimal** — Extensions are the minimum necessary to address the signal  
4. **Change is permanent record** — All changes are logged in IMP  
5. **Retroactive stability is preserved** — Prior objects retain governance version binding  
6. **HAN is the sole authorization authority** — No doctrine change without HAN review and approval

### Scope

| In Scope | Out of Scope |
| :---- | :---- |
| All stack instruments (ICC-8, AICA-5, AWOF, EAF, IMP, ILTP, CGF, ERDP, RGI-8, CAD-7, etc.) | Client engagement deliverables (CEF) |
| Signal identification and qualification | Business strategy or marketing |
| Change classification (4 classes) | Operational efficiency |
| Impact assessment | Technical delivery execution |
| HAN authorization | Commercial decisions |

### Governing Relationships

| Instrument | Relationship to DEP |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ICC-8** | Constitutional ceiling — DEP may not authorize changes that violate ICC-8 invariants; ICC-8 amendments require Class IV |
| **IMP** | Records all DEP proceedings as DROs and GAOs; doctrine evolution is institutional memory |
| **EAF** | Subject to DEP for amendment; EAF amendments require Class II or above |
| **AICA-5** | Subject to DEP for amendment; maturity grid revisions require Class II |
| **AWOF** | Subject to DEP for amendment; workforce authority changes require Class II |
| **ILTP** | Subject to DEP for amendment; structural layer changes require Class III |
| **CGF** | Subject to DEP for amendment; certification model changes require Class I or II |
| **ERDP** | Subject to DEP for amendment; reporting changes require Class I or II |
| **RGI-8** | Subject to DEP for amendment; execution mode changes require Class II |
| **CAD-7** | Subject to DEP for amendment; coalition model changes require Class II |
| **All future instruments** | Admitted to the canonical stack only through DEP Class I process |
| **HAN/HOF** | HAN is sole authorization authority for all DEP changes |

---

## SECTION 2: FOUNDATIONAL PRINCIPLES

| \# | Principle | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **P1** | **Doctrine Evolves From Evidence** | No framework, instrument, or position may be extended or amended based on preference, convenience, or commercial pressure alone. Every extension must be traceable to a documented signal. |
| **P2** | **The Stack Is a Constitutional System** | Instruments are components of a constitutional system. A change to one instrument may have downstream effects on others. DEP requires that all downstream effects be mapped before any amendment is authorized. |
| **P3** | **Minimum Necessary Change** | When a signal warrants doctrine evolution, the response is the minimum change necessary to address the signal. New frameworks are not created when an amendment to an existing instrument suffices. |
| **P4** | **Every Change Is Permanent Record** | Doctrine evolution is institutional memory. Every signal, evaluation, decision, and version change is recorded in IMP. No change is made off-record. |
| **P5** | **Retroactive Stability** | DEP changes do not retroactively alter prior engagements, decisions, or artifacts. All historical IMP objects retain their governance version binding. |
| **P6** | **HAN as Sole Authorization Authority** | No doctrine change of any class may be authorized without HAN review and approval. The AI operating architecture may identify signals, draft proposals, and conduct impact assessments — but authorization is a human accountability function that may not be delegated to AI. |

---

## SECTION 3: EXTENSION SIGNAL TYPES

### Overview

A valid doctrine extension process begins with a signal. Signals are the empirical inputs that justify evaluating whether doctrine evolution is warranted. There are five recognized signal types.

| \# | Signal Type | Description | Example |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **Engagement Gap** | Signal arising from an active or completed client engagement where the existing framework stack produced an incomplete, ambiguous, or contradictory output. Must be documented as OEO or DRO. | Engagement reveals AICA-5 does not address a specific class of autonomous agent deployment increasingly common in the client sector. |
| **2** | **External Environment Change** | Material change in regulatory environment, technology landscape, or institutional governance context rendering existing instrument incomplete or inconsistent with current conditions. | New AI governance regulation enacted in a jurisdiction where 19 Integrated operates. Existing CEF engagement terms do not address new compliance obligations. |
| **3** | **Internal Contradiction** | Logical inconsistency between two or more instruments producing conflicting outputs when applied simultaneously to the same engagement context. | IMP's provenance chain standard and AWOF's delegation rules produce conflicting requirements for hybrid AI-human decision records. |
| **4** | **Stress-Test Failure** | Scenario stress-test against any instrument produces a failure mode the current instrument cannot govern. May be identified through client engagement, internal review, or deliberate scenario analysis. | Stress-test of EAF's Tier 4 monitoring permissions reveals scenario where AI operating architecture could infer sensitive personnel information from aggregate organizational data without explicit consent. |
| **5** | **New Capability or Domain** | New institutional capability, service domain, or operational method not governed by any existing instrument. | 19 Integrated develops a drift detection methodology. No existing instrument governs the measurement logic, threshold definitions, or alert protocols. |

---

## SECTION 4: SIGNAL QUALIFICATION STANDARD

### Standard

Not every observation qualifies as a DEP signal. A signal must meet the qualification standard before it enters the DEP process.

| \# | Criteria | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **Specificity** | The signal identifies a specific gap, contradiction, failure mode, or unaddressed domain. General observations that "the framework could be improved" do not qualify. |
| **2** | **Evidence Basis** | The signal is grounded in a documented source: an IMP object (OEO, DRO, XOO), an external regulatory text, a named stress-test scenario, or a defined new capability. |
| **3** | **Non-Redundancy** | The signal addresses something not already addressed by an existing instrument or a signal already in the DEP process. |
| **4** | **Stack Relevance** | The signal relates to the governance of 19 Integrated's institutional operating architecture, not to a specific client deliverable. Client-specific gaps are addressed through the engagement process. Signals that reveal systemic gaps in the stack are DEP signals. |

### Qualification Process

| Step | Action | Responsible | Timeline |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Signal documented in IMP (as observation note on relevant OEO, DRO, or as standalone observation) | Any | Upon identification |
| 2 | Signal assessed against qualification standard | Node Steward (Ac-N5) | Within 14 days |
| 3 | If qualified → enter DEP process | Node Steward (Ac-N5) | Upon qualification |
| 4 | If not qualified → logged as observation; process ends | Node Steward (Ac-N5) | Upon determination |

### IMP Logging

| Object | Type | Content |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **OEO** | `outcome_type: "signal_identification"` | Signal documented |
| **DRO** | `decision_type: "framework_selection"` | Qualification determination |

---

## SECTION 5: CHANGE CLASSIFICATION

### Overview

Every proposed doctrine change is classified into one of four classes. The class determines the authorization requirements, the impact assessment scope, and the IMP recording standard.

| \# | Class | Definition | Examples |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **I** | **Clarification** | Resolves ambiguity, corrects error, or adds specificity to an existing instrument without altering substantive rules, scope, or governing relationships | Adding missing field definition to IMP object type; clarifying ambiguous term in EAF's intake doctrine; correcting internal cross-reference error; adding example to illustrate existing rule |
| **II** | **Amendment** | Modifies substantive rules, scope, permissions, or governing relationships of an existing instrument without altering foundational architecture or constitutional position | Adding new trust tier condition to EAF; expanding IMP's canonical object types with new field; revising AICA-5's maturity scoring dimensions; updating AWOF's delegation authority thresholds; adding new HAN trigger condition to EAF's trigger register |
| **III** | **Structural Extension** | Adds a new instrument to the canonical stack, fundamentally restructures an existing instrument's architecture, or alters governing relationships between instruments | Admitting new instrument to canonical stack; restructuring IMP's canonical object types (adding or retiring object type); altering EAF's trust tier architecture; redefining governing relationships between existing instruments; extending stack to new service domain or operational context |
| **IV** | **Constitutional Amendment** | Change to ICC-8 or to any instrument's relationship to ICC-8, or any change that alters fundamental constitutional architecture | Amending any ICC-8 invariant; changing what constitutes a constitutional violation; altering relationship between ICC-8 and any other instrument; redefining primitive layer (Trust/Memory/Action) architecture; any change that would alter foundational product thesis of 19 Integrated |

---

## SECTION 6: IMPACT ASSESSMENT REQUIREMENTS

| Class | Assessment Scope | Documentation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Class I** | Affected instrument only | DRO per determination |
| **Class II** | All referencing instruments; all affected instruments must be identified and consequential amendments mapped | DRO per determination |
| **Class III** | Full stack; every instrument in canonical stack assessed for impact; instruments requiring consequential amendments, version notation only, or no impact identified | GAO impact assessment document \+ DRO per determination |
| **Class IV** | Full constitutional impact assessment; every instrument in canonical stack; every active client engagement; every IMP object produced under prior constitutional state; assessment identifies whether prior objects remain valid under proposed change or require reissuance | GAO constitutional impact assessment document \+ DRO per determination |

---

## SECTION 7: DEP PROCESS FLOW

SIGNAL IDENTIFICATION  
└── Signal observed (engagement gap, external change, contradiction,  
    stress-test failure, or new capability)  
└── Signal documented in IMP (as observation note on relevant OEO,  
    DRO, or as standalone CRO)

SIGNAL QUALIFICATION  
└── Signal assessed against qualification standard  
    (specificity, evidence basis, non-redundancy, stack relevance)  
└── Qualified → enter DEP process  
└── Not qualified → logged as observation; process ends

CHANGE CLASSIFICATION  
└── Proposed change classified (Class I / II / III / IV)  
└── Classification documented as DRO

IMPACT ASSESSMENT  
└── Class I: affected instrument only  
└── Class II: all referencing instruments  
└── Class III: full stack  
└── Class IV: full constitutional assessment  
└── Impact assessment documented (DRO for each determination;  
    GAO for Class III and IV assessment documents)  
DELIBERATION PERIOD  
└── Class I: none required  
└── Class II: minimum 48 hours  
└── Class III: minimum 7 days  
└── Class IV: minimum 30 days \+ 8-scenario stress test

HAN REVIEW AND AUTHORIZATION  
└── HAN reviews signal, classification, impact assessment,  
    and proposed change  
└── HAN authorizes / modifies / rejects  
└── Authorization documented as DRO (han\_review\_flag: true,  
    han\_outcome: approved / modified / rejected)

INSTRUMENT REVISION  
└── Affected instrument(s) revised  
└── Version increments applied per classification  
└── Governing framework version map updated

IMP RECORDING  
└── All DEP objects recorded per classification standard  
└── Governance version binding updated across all affected objects  
    for forward-dated engagements

NOTIFICATION  
└── Active engagements at affected trust tiers notified of  
    version change in their ECO  
└── No retroactive alteration to historical objects  
---

| Class | Deliberation Period | Stress Test Requirement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Class I** | None required | Not required |
| **Class II** | Minimum 48 hours between signal qualification and authorization | Not required |
| **Class III** | Minimum 7 days between signal qualification and authorization | Not required |
| **Class IV** | Minimum 30 days between signal qualification and authorization | Minimum 8 scenarios |

## SECTION 11: DEP SELF-REFERENCE PROVISION

### Rule

DEP governs its own amendment. Changes to DEP are subject to DEP's own process.

| Change Scope | Classification |
| :---- | :---- |
| Clarification of DEP language | Class I |
| Amendment to signal types, qualification standard, or change classification definitions | Class II |
| Structural change to DEP process flow | Class III |
| Any change that alters DEP's relationship to ICC-8 | Class IV |

### Prohibition

DEP may not be amended in a manner that reduces the authorization requirements for any change class. Authorization requirements may only be increased through DEP amendment, never decreased, except through a Class IV constitutional amendment with full deliberation.

# Regulatory Overlay — EU AI Act v1.0

**Status:** Built — v1.0  
**Type:** Compliance Instrument  
**Parent Stack:** AIGIS Compliance Engine  
**Version:** 1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The EU AI Act Regulatory Overlay is the authoritative mapping between AIGIS controls and the European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act. It answers: *How does every AIGIS control map to specific articles of the EU AI Act, and what are the coverage gaps?*

This overlay operationalizes the EU AI Act within the AIGIS Compliance Engine. It provides a complete mapping of all 109 MCR controls to the relevant articles of the EU AI Act, including Title I (General Provisions), Title II (Prohibited AI Practices), Title III (High-Risk AI Systems), Title IV (Transparency Obligations), and Title V (General-Purpose AI). The overlay includes gap analysis, article-by-article coverage, and implementation recommendations.

**The core insight:** The EU AI Act is the world's first comprehensive AI law. AIGIS compliance with the EU AI Act is not optional for organizations operating in or serving the EU market. This overlay makes AIGIS provably compliant with the EU AI Act at every control level.

---

## SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND SCOPE

### Purpose

The EU AI Act Overlay ensures that:

1. **Every AIGIS control is mapped** — All 109 MCR controls map to EU AI Act articles  
2. **Coverage is complete** — All relevant EU AI Act articles are covered  
3. **Gaps are visible** — Uncovered articles are identified  
4. **Implementation is traceable** — Each article maps to implementing controls  
5. **Compliance is demonstrable** — Evidence requirements are defined

| All 109 MCR controls | Non-AIGIS controls |
| All relevant EU AI Act articles (1-113) | Non-EU frameworks |

| Implementation mapping | Certification process |
| Evidence requirements | Enforcement mechanisms |

@dataclass  
class EUAIMapping:  
    """EU AI Act mapping for a single article"""  
    article: EUAIArticle  
    title: str  
    description: str  
    mcr\_control\_ids: List\[str\]  
    coverage: str  \# Full / Partial / None  
    evidence\_required: bool  
    evidence\_type: str

class EUAIOverlay:  
    """EU AI Act Regulatory Overlay"""  
      
    def \_\_init\_\_(self):  
        self.mappings: Dict\[EUAIArticle, EUAIMapping\] \= {}  
        self.\_build\_mappings()  
      
    def \_build\_mappings(self):  
        """Build all article mappings"""

        self.mappings\[EUAIArticle.ART\_1\] \= EUAIMapping(

    def get\_mapping(self, article: EUAIArticle) \-\> Optional\[EUAIMapping\]:  
        """Get mapping for a specific article"""  
        return self.mappings.get(article)  
      
    def get\_controls\_for\_article(self, article: EUAIArticle) \-\> List\[str\]:  
        """Get MCR control IDs for a specific article"""  
        mapping \= self.mappings.get(article)  
        if not mapping:  
            return \[\]  
        return mapping.mcr\_control\_ids  
      
    def get\_articles\_for\_control(self, control\_id: str) \-\> List\[str\]:  
        """Get articles that map to a specific control"""  
        result \= \[\]  
        for mapping in self.mappings.values():  
            if control\_id in mapping.mcr\_control\_ids:  
                result.append(mapping.article.value)  
        return result  
      
    def get\_gap\_analysis(self) \-\> Dict:  
        """Get gap analysis for EU AI Act"""  
        total \= len(self.mappings)  
        full \= sum(1 for m in self.mappings.values() if m.coverage \== "Full")  
        partial \= sum(1 for m in self.mappings.values() if m.coverage \== "Partial")  
        none \= sum(1 for m in self.mappings.values() if m.coverage \== "None")  
          
        return {  
            "total\_articles": total,  
            "full\_coverage": full,  
            "partial\_coverage": partial,  
            "no\_coverage": none,  
            "coverage\_pct": (full / total) \* 100 if total \> 0 else 0,  
            "partial\_articles": \[m.article.value for m in self.mappings.values()   
                                if m.coverage \== "Partial"\],  
            "uncovered\_articles": \[m.article.value for m in self.mappings.values()   
                                  if m.coverage \== "None"\]  
        }  
      
    def get\_evidence\_summary(self) \-\> Dict:  
        """Get evidence requirements summary"""  
        evidence\_types \= {}  
        for mapping in self.mappings.values():  
            if mapping.evidence\_required:  
                evidence\_types\[mapping.evidence\_type\] \= evidence\_types.get(mapping.evidence\_type, 0\) \+ 1  
        return evidence\_types  
      
    def export\_overlay(self, format: str \= "json") \-\> str:  
        """Export the overlay in requested format"""  
        if format \== "json":  
            import json  
            return json.dumps({  
                "framework": "eu\_ai\_act",  
                "version": "1.0",  
                "mappings": {  
                    m.article.value: {  
                        "title": m.title,  
                        "description": m.description,  
                        "mcr\_control\_ids": m.mcr\_control\_ids,  
                        "coverage": m.coverage,  
                        "evidence\_required": m.evidence\_required,  
                        "evidence\_type": m.evidence\_type  
                    } for m in self.mappings.values()  
                }  
            }, indent=2)  
        return ""

## SECTION 5: USAGE EXAMPLES

### 5.1 Basic Usage

\# Initialize the EU AI Act overlay  
eu\_ai \= EUAIOverlay()

\# Get mapping for Article 14 (Human Oversight)  
mapping \= eu\_ai.get\_mapping(EUAIArticle.ART\_14)  
print(f"Article: {mapping.article.value} — {mapping.title}")  
print(f"Description: {mapping.description}")  
print(f"MCR Controls: {mapping.mcr\_control\_ids}")  
print(f"Coverage: {mapping.coverage}")

\# Get articles for a specific control  
articles \= eu\_ai.get\_articles\_for\_control("AICA-5-CN-014")  
print(f"Articles for AICA-5-CN-014: {articles}")

\# Get gap analysis  
gap \= eu\_ai.get\_gap\_analysis()  
print(f"Coverage: {gap\['coverage\_pct'\]}%")  
print(f"Partial articles: {gap\['partial\_articles'\]}")

\# Get evidence requirements  
evidence \= eu\_ai.get\_evidence\_summary()  
print(f"Evidence types: {evidence}")

### 5.2 Compliance Checklist

\# Get compliance checklist  
checklist \= eu\_ai.get\_compliance\_checklist()  
for category, articles in checklist.items():  
    print(f"\\n{category} ({len(articles)} articles)")  
    for article in articles:  
        mapping \= eu\_ai.get\_mapping(EUAIArticle(article))  
        status \= "✅" if mapping.coverage \== "Full" else "⚠️" if mapping.coverage \== "Partial" else "❌"  
        print(f"  {status} {article}: {mapping.title}")

### 5.3 Integration with Crosswalk Engine

from compliance\_crosswalk\_engine import ComplianceCrosswalkEngine  
from master\_control\_registry import MasterControlRegistry

mcr \= MasterControlRegistry()  
crosswalk \= ComplianceCrosswalkEngine(registry=mcr)  
eu\_ai \= EUAIOverlay()

\# Map an article to MCR controls  
article \= EUAIArticle.ART\_14  
controls \= eu\_ai.get\_controls\_for\_article(article)  
print(f"Article {article.value} maps to {len(controls)} controls:")

\# Cross-reference with crosswalk engine  
for control\_id in controls:  
    mappings \= crosswalk.map\_component\_to\_framework(control\_id, "eu\_ai\_act")  
    for m in mappings:  
        print(f"  {control\_id} → {m.clause}: {m.clause\_description}")

# Regulatory Overlay — NIST AI RMF v1.0

**Status:** Built — v1.0  
**Type:** Compliance Instrument  
**Parent Stack:** AIGIS Compliance Engine  
**Version:** 1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The NIST AI RMF Regulatory Overlay is the authoritative mapping between AIGIS controls and the National Institute of Standards and Technology's Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework. It answers: *How does every AIGIS control map to the four functions of the NIST AI RMF — GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE?*

This overlay operationalizes the NIST AI RMF within the AIGIS Compliance Engine. It provides a complete mapping of all 109 MCR controls to the NIST AI RMF's four functions, categories, and subcategories. The overlay includes gap analysis, function-by-function coverage, and implementation recommendations.

**The core insight:** The NIST AI RMF is the leading voluntary framework for AI risk management in the United States and globally. AIGIS compliance with the NIST AI RMF demonstrates alignment with international best practices and provides a credible foundation for regulatory compliance across multiple jurisdictions.

---

## SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND SCOPE

### Purpose

The NIST AI RMF Overlay ensures that:

1. **Every AIGIS control is mapped** — All 109 MCR controls map to NIST AI RMF functions  
2. **Coverage is complete** — All relevant NIST AI RMF categories and subcategories are covered  
3. **Gaps are visible** — Uncovered categories are identified  
4. **Implementation is traceable** — Each function maps to implementing controls  
5. **Compliance is demonstrable** — Evidence requirements are defined

### Scope

| In Scope | Out of Scope |
| :---- | :---- |
| All 109 MCR controls | Non-AIGIS controls |
| NIST AI RMF four functions (GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE) | Other NIST frameworks |
| NIST AI RMF categories and subcategories | Legal interpretation |
| Gap analysis | Certification process |
| Implementation mapping | Enforcement mechanisms |

### NIST AI RMF Structure

| Function | Description | Categories |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **GOVERN** | Establish governance and accountability | 3 categories |
| **MAP** | Map and contextualize | 4 categories |
| **MEASURE** | Measure and evaluate | 4 categories |
| **MANAGE** | Manage and mitigate | 4 categories |

    """NIST AI RMF Function Enumeration"""  
    GOVERN \= "GOVERN"  
    MAP \= "MAP"  
    MEASURE \= "MEASURE"  
    MANAGE \= "MANAGE"

class NISTCategory(Enum):  
    """NIST AI RMF Category Enumeration"""  
    \# GOVERN  
    GV\_1 \= "GV-1"  
    GV\_2 \= "GV-2"  
    GV\_3 \= "GV-3"  
    GV\_4 \= "GV-4"  
    \# MAP  
    MP\_1 \= "MP-1"  
    MP\_2 \= "MP-2"  
    MP\_3 \= "MP-3"  
    MP\_4 \= "MP-4"  
    \# MEASURE

    MS\_3 \= "MS-3"  
    MS\_4 \= "MS-4"  
    \# MANAGE  
    MG\_1 \= "MG-1"  
    MG\_2 \= "MG-2"  
    MG\_3 \= "MG-3"  
    MG\_4 \= "MG-4"

@dataclass  
class NISTMapping:  
    """NIST AI RMF mapping for a single subcategory"""  
    category: NISTCategory  
    function: NISTFunction  
    title: str  
    description: str

    def get\_mapping(self, category: NISTCategory) \-\> Optional\[NISTMapping\]:  
        """Get mapping for a specific subcategory"""  
        return self.mappings.get(category)  
      
    def get\_controls\_for\_category(self, category: NISTCategory) \-\> List\[str\]:  
        """Get MCR control IDs for a specific category"""  
        mapping \= self.mappings.get(category)  
        if not mapping:  
            return \[\]  
        return mapping.mcr\_control\_ids  
      
    def get\_controls\_for\_function(self, function: NISTFunction) \-\> List\[str\]:  
        """Get MCR control IDs for all categories in a function"""  
        result \= \[\]  
        for mapping in self.mappings.values():  
            if mapping.function \== function:  
                result.extend(mapping.mcr\_control\_ids)  
        return list(set(result))  
      
    def get\_categories\_for\_control(self, control\_id: str) \-\> List\[str\]:  
        """Get categories that map to a specific control"""  
        result \= \[\]  
        for mapping in self.mappings.values():  
            if control\_id in mapping.mcr\_control\_ids:  
                result.append(mapping.category.value)  
        return result  
      
    def get\_gap\_analysis(self) \-\> Dict:  
        """Get gap analysis for NIST AI RMF"""  
        total \= len(self.mappings)  
        full \= sum(1 for m in self.mappings.values() if m.coverage \== "Full")  
        partial \= sum(1 for m in self.mappings.values() if m.coverage \== "Partial")  
        none \= sum(1 for m in self.mappings.values() if m.coverage \== "None")  
          
        return {  
            "total\_subcategories": total,  
            "full\_coverage": full,  
            "partial\_coverage": partial,  
            "no\_coverage": none,  
            "coverage\_pct": (full / total) \* 100 if total \> 0 else 0,  
            "partial\_subcategories": \[m.category.value for m in self.mappings.values()   
                                      if m.coverage \== "Partial"\],  
            "uncovered\_subcategories": \[m.category.value for m in self.mappings.values()   
                                        if m.coverage \== "None"\]  
        }  
      
    def get\_function\_summary(self) \-\> Dict:  
        """Get summary by function"""  
        summary \= {}  
        for function in NISTFunction:  
            controls \= self.get\_controls\_for\_function(function)  
            categories \= \[m for m in self.mappings.values() if m.function \== function\]  
            summary\[function.value\] \= {  
                "total\_categories": len(categories),  
                "full\_coverage": sum(1 for m in categories if m.coverage \== "Full"),  
                "total\_controls": len(controls),  
                "unique\_controls": len(set(controls))  
            }  
        return summary  
      
    def get\_evidence\_summary(self) \-\> Dict:  
        """Get evidence requirements summary"""  
        evidence\_types \= {}  
        for mapping in self.mappings.values():  
            if mapping.evidence\_required:  
                evidence\_types\[mapping.evidence\_type\] \= evidence\_types.get(mapping.evidence\_type, 0\) \+ 1  
        return evidence\_types  
      
    def export\_overlay(self, format: str \= "json") \-\> str:  
        """Export the overlay in requested format"""  
        if format \== "json":  
            import json  
            return json.dumps({  
                "framework": "nist\_ai\_rmf",  
                "version": "1.0",  
                "mappings": {  
                    m.category.value: {  
                        "function": m.function.value,  
                        "title": m.title,  
                        "description": m.description,  
                        "mcr\_control\_ids": m.mcr\_control\_ids,  
                        "coverage": m.coverage,  
                        "evidence\_required": m.evidence\_required,  
                        "evidence\_type": m.evidence\_type  
                    } for m in self.mappings.values()  
                }  
            }, indent=2)  
        return ""  
      
    def get\_compliance\_checklist(self) \-\> Dict\[str, List\[str\]\]:  
        """Get a compliance checklist by function"""  
        checklist \= {  
            "GOVERN": \[\],  
            "MAP": \[\],  
            "MEASURE": \[\],  
            "MANAGE": \[\]  
        }  
          
        for mapping in self.mappings.values():  
            checklist\[mapping.function.value\].append(mapping.category.value)  
          
        return checklist

## SECTION 5: USAGE EXAMPLES

### 5.1 Basic Usage

\# Initialize the NIST AI RMF overlay  
nist \= NISTAIRMFOverlay()

\# Get mapping for GV-2 (Accountability)  
mapping \= nist.get\_mapping(NISTCategory.GV\_2)  
print(f"Category: {mapping.category.value} — {mapping.title}")  
print(f"Function: {mapping.function.value}")  
print(f"Description: {mapping.description}")  
print(f"MCR Controls: {mapping.mcr\_control\_ids}")  
print(f"Coverage: {mapping.coverage}")

\# Get categories for a specific control  
categories \= nist.get\_categories\_for\_control("HOF-H1")  
print(f"Categories for HOF-H1: {categories}")

\# Get gap analysis  
gap \= nist.get\_gap\_analysis()  
print(f"Coverage: {gap\['coverage\_pct'\]}%")  
print(f"Total subcategories: {gap\['total\_subcategories'\]}")

### 5.2 Function Summary

\# Get function summary  
summary \= nist.get\_function\_summary()  
for function, data in summary.items():  
    print(f"\\n{function}:")  
    print(f"  Categories: {data\['total\_categories'\]}")  
    print(f"  Full coverage: {data\['full\_coverage'\]}")  
    print(f"  Total controls: {data\['total\_controls'\]}")  
    print(f"  Unique controls: {data\['unique\_controls'\]}")

### 5.3 Compliance Checklist

\# Get compliance checklist  
checklist \= nist.get\_compliance\_checklist()  
for function, categories in checklist.items():  
    print(f"\\n{function} Function ({len(categories)} categories):")  
    for category in categories:  
        mapping \= nist.get\_mapping(NISTCategory(category))  
        status \= "✅" if mapping.coverage \== "Full" else "⚠️"  
        print(f"  {status} {category}: {mapping.title}")

### 5.4 Integration with Crosswalk Engine

from compliance\_crosswalk\_engine import ComplianceCrosswalkEngine  
from master\_control\_registry import MasterControlRegistry

mcr \= MasterControlRegistry()  
crosswalk \= ComplianceCrosswalkEngine(registry=mcr)  
nist \= NISTAIRMFOverlay()

\# Map a category to MCR controls  
category \= NISTCategory.GV\_2  
controls \= nist.get\_controls\_for\_category(category)  
print(f"Category {category.value} maps to {len(controls)} controls:")  
print(f"  {', '.join(controls)}")

# Regulatory Overlay — Philippines v1.0

**Status:** Built — v1.0  
**Type:** Compliance Instrument  
**Parent Stack:** AIGIS Compliance Engine  
**Version:** 1.0

---

## PREAMBLE

The Philippines Regulatory Overlay is the authoritative mapping between AIGIS controls and the Philippine regulatory frameworks governing AI, sustainability, data privacy, and financial services. It answers: *How does every AIGIS control map to Philippine regulations including PFRS S1/S2, BSP STARS, DICT-CSC JMC 003, and NPC Advisory 2024-04?*

This overlay operationalizes Philippine regulatory compliance within the AIGIS Compliance Engine. It provides complete mapping of all 109 MCR controls to the four primary Philippine frameworks that govern AI deployment and data governance. The overlay includes gap analysis, framework-by-framework coverage, and implementation recommendations specific to the Philippine regulatory environment.

**The core insight:** The Philippines is rapidly developing an AI governance ecosystem through multiple regulatory channels — sustainability reporting (PFRS S1/S2), financial services AI governance (BSP STARS), government AI use (DICT-CSC JMC 003), and data privacy (NPC Advisory 2024-04). AIGIS compliance with these frameworks is essential for organizations operating in or serving the Philippine market.

---

## SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND SCOPE

### Purpose

The Philippines Overlay ensures that:

1. **Every AIGIS control is mapped** — All 109 MCR controls map to Philippine frameworks  
2. **Coverage is complete** — All relevant Philippine regulatory requirements are covered  
3. **Gaps are visible** — Uncovered requirements are identified  
4. **Implementation is traceable** — Each requirement maps to implementing controls  
5. **Compliance is demonstrable** — Evidence requirements are defined

### Scope

| In Scope | Out of Scope |
| :---- | :---- |
| All 109 MCR controls | Non-AIGIS controls |
| PFRS S1/S2 (SEC MC No. 16-2025) | Other Philippine regulations |
| BSP STARS AI Governance | Legal interpretation |
| DICT-CSC JMC 003 | Certification process |
| NPC Advisory 2024-04 | Enforcement mechanisms |

| **BSP STARS** | BSP | TBD | AI governance for financial institutions |
| **DICT-CSC JMC 003** | DICT/CSC | TBD | AI use in government |

    def get\_mappings\_for\_framework(self, framework: PhilippinesFramework) \-\> List\[PhilippinesMapping\]:  
        """Get all mappings for a specific framework"""  
        return \[m for m in self.mappings if m.framework \== framework\]  
      
    def get\_controls\_for\_framework(self, framework: PhilippinesFramework) \-\> List\[str\]:  
        """Get all MCR control IDs for a specific framework"""  
        result \= \[\]  
        for mapping in self.get\_mappings\_for\_framework(framework):  
            result.extend(mapping.mcr\_control\_ids)  
        return list(set(result))  
      
    def get\_mappings\_for\_control(self, control\_id: str) \-\> List\[PhilippinesMapping\]:  
        """Get all mappings for a specific control"""  
        return \[m for m in self.mappings if control\_id in m.mcr\_control\_ids\]  
      
    def get\_framework\_summary(self) \-\> Dict:  
        """Get summary by framework"""  
        summary \= {}  
        for framework in PhilippinesFramework:  
            mappings \= self.get\_mappings\_for\_framework(framework)  
            unique\_controls \= set()  
            for m in mappings:  
                unique\_controls.update(m.mcr\_control\_ids)  
            summary\[framework.value\] \= {  
                "total\_requirements": len(mappings),  
                "full\_coverage": sum(1 for m in mappings if m.coverage \== "Full"),  
                "partial\_coverage": sum(1 for m in mappings if m.coverage \== "Partial"),  
                "total\_controls": len(unique\_controls)  
            }  
        return summary  
      
    def get\_gap\_analysis(self) \-\> Dict:  
        """Get gap analysis for all Philippine frameworks"""  
        total \= len(self.mappings)  
        full \= sum(1 for m in self.mappings if m.coverage \== "Full")  
        partial \= sum(1 for m in self.mappings if m.coverage \== "Partial")  
        none \= sum(1 for m in self.mappings if m.coverage \== "None")  
          
        return {  
            "total\_requirements": total,  
            "full\_coverage": full,  
            "partial\_coverage": partial,  
            "no\_coverage": none,  
            "coverage\_pct": (full / total) \* 100 if total \> 0 else 0,  
            "by\_framework": self.get\_framework\_summary()  
        }  
      
    def get\_evidence\_summary(self) \-\> Dict:  
        """Get evidence requirements summary"""  
        evidence\_types \= {}  
        for mapping in self.mappings:  
            if mapping.evidence\_required:  
                evidence\_types\[mapping.evidence\_type\] \= evidence\_types.get(mapping.evidence\_type, 0\) \+ 1  
        return evidence\_types  
      
    def export\_overlay(self, format: str \= "json") \-\> str:  
        """Export the overlay in requested format"""  
        if format \== "json":  
            import json  
            return json.dumps({  
                "framework": "philippines",  
                "version": "1.0",  
                "mappings": \[{  
                    "framework": m.framework.value,  
                    "requirement\_id": m.requirement\_id,  
                    "requirement\_title": m.requirement\_title,  
                    "description": m.description,  
                    "mcr\_control\_ids": m.mcr\_control\_ids,  
                    "coverage": m.coverage,  
                    "evidence\_required": m.evidence\_required,  
                    "evidence\_type": m.evidence\_type  
                } for m in self.mappings\]  
            }, indent=2)  
        return ""  
      
    def get\_compliance\_checklist(self) \-\> Dict\[str, List\[str\]\]:  
        """Get a compliance checklist by framework"""  
        checklist \= {  
            "PFRS S1/S2": \[\],  
            "BSP STARS": \[\],  
            "DICT-CSC JMC 003": \[\],  
            "NPC Advisory 2024-04": \[\]  
        }  
          
        framework\_names \= {  
            PhilippinesFramework.PFRS\_S1\_S2: "PFRS S1/S2",  
            PhilippinesFramework.BSP\_STARS: "BSP STARS",  
            PhilippinesFramework.DICT\_CSC\_JMC\_003: "DICT-CSC JMC 003",  
            PhilippinesFramework.NPC\_ADVISORY\_2024\_04: "NPC Advisory 2024-04"  
        }  
          
        for mapping in self.mappings:  
            name \= framework\_names.get(mapping.framework, mapping.framework.value)  
            checklist\[name\].append(mapping.requirement\_id)  
          
        return checklist

\# Initialize the Philippines overlay
